attributes.title: ee0e011c-af09-4ab4-ade4-fa04f78159ce
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.165
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.          dimly through morning/ mists over Akashi Bay my/ longings trace the ship/ vanishing from sight 	floating/ silently behind the isle

attributes.title: d59b7f7f-ceff-42ef-aa36-027fd15a23f0
attributes.field_text: Although my abode lies not in Harima bay, will my lover part without even waiting for daybreak.

attributes.title: d9bbf9bf-c71e-42c8-b6cc-483302a2952c
attributes.field_text: I wonder how the sky above the capital might be. Even tonight when I regard the bright moon in Akashi.

attributes.title: c24ef099-8291-4a42-92ab-83c59866eecb
attributes.field_text: The moon at dawn shined brightly in Akashi, when in the wind from the bay I saw only the waves approaching

attributes.title: 85617c82-aa1f-48e1-b3d4-045d4e05e2bf
attributes.field_text: Composed on the conception of the moon by the sea.          Gazing out/ I find my heart’s last hope/ Is not gone;/ Above the offing at Akashi bright and/ Clear is the moonlight

attributes.title: 207c0284-6fb7-4ff4-be4e-e9b4c05286c6
attributes.field_text: Composed on the topic “nightingale at the seashore”        unless I hear/ a second song I'll not set sail/  nightingale no matter/ how many nights I must moor/ awake till dawn at Akashi

attributes.title: f65b1563-f78b-4408-8572-3d1637db4b68
attributes.field_text: For the “Fifteen-Hundred-Round Poetry Contest”.                   in anguished yearning/ I await break of day at/ Akashi Bay 	plovers/ On the waves 	crying out I/  Weep on a tear-drenched pillow

attributes.title: b41a2013-5f31-417e-aa76-bcf04498c498
attributes.field_text: On the topic ‘the moon at the seashore’ for a Poetry Bureau poetry contest.      Akashi Lagoon/ ah 	look at the colorless/ sleeves of unfeeling/ fisherfolk 	could the moon chose/ its lodging so capriciously

attributes.title: 3c3f64c2-262e-4143-94c2-2a07d994b0aa
attributes.field_text: Composed about Akashi Bay.     on roofs of the small/ fishing boats where rush mats flap/ in winds from the bay/ of Akashi 	alone I/ gaze at the moon till daybreak

attributes.title: 0e361d77-d5a7-46b2-8aab-98888f6e99e1
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.     rowing back along/ the long roads from provinces/ distant as the sky/ from the Strait of Akashi/ Yamato islands are seen

attributes.title: c8406a56-4de7-4040-ad42-935bbfe9cf67
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.253
attributes.field_text: smoke from the salt fires/ of the Suma fisherfolk/ buffeted by fierce/ winds 	sways and drifts away in/ unexpected directions

attributes.title: 0de20e57-fa8c-4caa-8ea6-f552c4823d55
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.267
attributes.field_text: widely spaced 	woven/ with a broad shuttle 	are the/ threads of the robes worn/ by the Suma fisherfolk/ and the visits of my love

attributes.title: f834f799-ed3e-4daf-9fdf-93c782fed51b
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.325-326
attributes.field_text: if from time to time/ anyone should ask after/  me 	answer them this/ on Suma Bay with tear-drenched/ sleeves I gather seaweed salt

attributes.title: 1fb737c6-5e8d-4a6d-ab40-abf3ecdcd0bd
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.39
attributes.field_text: Perhaps this poem is a better example: smoke from the salt fires/  of the Suma fisherfolk/ buffeted by fierce/ winds 	sways and drifts away in/  unexpected directions

attributes.title: a9908304-46c9-4345-8260-022810e8cc1a
attributes.field_text: Those plovers crying/ between Awaji Isle and land  ̶   / how many long nights/ do they keep the guards from sleep/  at their posts on Suma’s shore.

attributes.title: ec2c6c36-e6cf-4572-92f9-e09cf39acf48
attributes.field_text: garments wet by the waves/ fisherfolk of Suma 	once/ I had thought myself/ a stranger to those splashing/ drops 	but now they strike me too

attributes.title: b1eac195-90b5-46d1-90d2-e146b7fe4111
attributes.field_text: at Suma Bay 	as/ piercing as the salty scent/ of wood piled high by/ fisherfolk who gather salt  ̶  / this flame that smolders in me

attributes.title: 9c6c5ac0-1086-4a09-a8d0-87439db7f9a3
attributes.field_text: for me naught but love/ fisherfolk of Suma Bay/ seaweed salt drips on/ sleeves that never dry 	ah 	to/ know what will become of them

attributes.title: 957fb067-900c-4a2b-a796-3120366e9a95
attributes.field_text: Suma fisherfolk/ grow accustomed to the sound/ of the salt wind that/ buffets their billowing sleeves/ yet no hand can ever grasp it

attributes.title: 504ca339-24cf-4363-828b-c71fe6f09971
attributes.field_text: growing close only/ leads to sorrow in this world  ̶  / Suma seafolk 	their/ salt-making robes have coarse threads/  as widely spaced as our meetings

attributes.title: 878401ae-7e50-4af1-bd9c-220f61ff56aa
attributes.field_text: though white waves rise in/ noisy outcry at Suma/ Bay 	where they harvest/ seaweed 	still unabashed 	I/  will continue to see you

attributes.title: c3c7b41f-f186-425e-8f37-339c76b9109c
attributes.field_text: sleeves dipping 	salt tides/ reflect the moon 	surely they would/ never willingly/ greet the dawn anywhere but/ here 	people of Suma Bay

attributes.title: 1f89126e-33d7-4e0d-8bb2-00d22f7ad901
attributes.field_text: at Suma Bay on/ a quiet windless morning/ in spring 	my eyes glimpse/ in the distance 	fishing boats/ veiled by a curtain of mist

attributes.title: 3828c428-4142-4418-a8e9-7efc0e4d7f79
attributes.field_text: each time I feel that/ cold wind of autumn blowing/ through the barrier/ pounding waves on Suma Bay/ add their resonant voices

attributes.title: 99b6d8a6-81cb-4f69-a371-cfc129396a2e
attributes.field_text: Suma barrier/ never giving a thought to/ the crashing of waves/ that keep dreams from wandering/ I have taken lodging here

attributes.title: 4a326e9b-d52d-4181-9492-0af5277a704d
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.310
attributes.field_text: were they only men/ I would ask the youthful pines/ that deck the shores of/ Suminoe 	how many/  Generations they have seen

attributes.title: 78997383-b461-4ee0-a43a-c6fe9c2f2c2c
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.313
attributes.field_text: though fisherfolk say/ Sumiyoshi is a good/ place to live 	do not/ remain long 	for grasses of/ forgetfulness thrive there too

attributes.title: 8c2dc3e3-b6b0-4fbf-9a13-8cb026a884ca
attributes.field_text: At Sumiyoshi/  shore the white waves/  approach, night after night/  it is sad that the fisher is looking askance.

attributes.title: ede34c5a-3697-48f9-b3d0-501c0c51f5a3
attributes.field_text: If my body were like Sumiyoshi/  then even if the years passed/  would I really look at/  something other than a pine?

attributes.title: 2640d560-a86c-4b4f-a6c2-072bd2d80370
attributes.field_text: The white waves/  night by night nearing the cost/  rising up there/  though we have met before/  the Pine of Sumiyoshi.

attributes.title: 2f13f0da-e562-4304-8a4e-3af9ba68835d
attributes.field_text: At Sumiyoshi, a pleasant place,/ The pines are washed over/ By the whitecaps;/ With their retreat/ Are they left rootless, weeping wails?

attributes.title: d9e909d8-8c09-4b93-bcc5-404efb334d0f
attributes.field_text: The past/ We will abandon;/ From this year forth/ Of a thousand years in number make a pile,/ We pines of Sumiyoshi!

attributes.title: 5aaf177e-7637-408e-9cb7-26b544f73151
attributes.field_text: Furthermore, the god of Sumiyoshi left behind the words “the ridge logs of the shrine roof,” and Dengyō daishi spoke of his feelings on “climbing the timbered mountain.”

attributes.title: 0c3eca0f-298f-43bc-8bce-cd1d7874f6f3
attributes.field_text: still no moonlight can/  seep through the branches of pines/ at Sumiyoshi/ though the autumn wind rages/ attacking every last tree

attributes.title: 8dd67395-656c-4476-a777-7b99b489518a
attributes.field_text: if you offer your/ protection to our path 	you must/ then favor our lord/ as well 	please cede to him your/ years 	pine of Sumiyoshi

attributes.title: b6fd4b99-bb42-4d2a-b239-0fe1f664d1d2
attributes.field_text: how sad I am 	I/ who was born in this world where/ seeds of grasses of/ love’s forgetfulness no longer/ burgeon at Sumiyoshi

attributes.title: 67ec4c79-b117-4cf5-930b-f76c7ccc4ad7
attributes.field_text: although it may please/ the hearts of those who wait for/ you 	do not think no/ other place as pleasant to live/  as Sumiyoshi village

attributes.title: a76a8ad0-7a98-4552-ae6b-62e52e8c21d7
attributes.field_text: never could I feel/ the pines of Sumiyoshi/ were awaiting me/ I yearn still for the shelter of/ the thousand years of my lord

attributes.title: 4da3fb6c-86a8-4a26-82da-1d683de9622b
attributes.field_text: though sorrow-laden/ I’ve languished these many years/ in this sad world 	have/ the pines of Sumiyoshi/ protected me all this time

attributes.title: 6568bc9a-965b-47d2-9be8-f2be8453ddea
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.140
attributes.field_text: the swiftly driven/ snow 	falling into rough drifts/ near the shore 	looks like/ rows of crested waves crossing/ Suenomatsu Mountain

attributes.title: 05d0c5fb-58f1-467d-a332-cbf7545e93bc
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.372
attributes.field_text: if ever I should/ change my mind 	and banish you/ from my heart 	then would/  great ocean waves rise and cross/ Suenomatsu Mountain

attributes.title: a973c73c-1315-497d-a1d5-efa92b27e569
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.41
attributes.field_text: […], he might invoke the waves on Matsuyama, dip water from the meadow spring, gaze upon the underleaves of the autumn bush clover, count the flutterings of the wings of the snipe at dawn, […]

attributes.title: b39ab6df-3b9d-433a-aae6-8d0d80d53b2b
attributes.field_text: Journey piled on journey/ At a distance of a thousand years/ Will you see?/ From the pines of Sue,/ To the living pine groves.

attributes.title: e7528a1e-24b7-497e-9291-1cd443e0b8f1
attributes.field_text: Have you forgotten/  wringing tears from our sleeves  ̶   / vowing that our love/  would stand high above the waves/ like Pine Mountain in Sue?

attributes.title: 12c46971-151c-4f80-aaa3-b81936ebb798
attributes.field_text: What am I to do?/ If upon the pine-clad peak of Sué/ The waves should break,/ The first snows upon the peak/ Would vanish clear away!

attributes.title: 2a15059b-45d2-453f-bfc9-ea9b9de6ad5b
attributes.field_text: Your Majesty’s reign:/ Upon the pine-clad peak of Sué,/ So distant/ Break whitecaps/ In numbers unknown to all!

attributes.title: 369bee2c-3a05-42c4-8d41-472a5baa60d4
attributes.field_text: heavy mist rises/ veiling Suenomatsu/ Mountain 	dimly seen/ breaking away from the waves/  clouds trail sideways in the sky

attributes.title: 1dd5a966-4dbb-4e41-8252-2c3a07999e01
attributes.field_text: waves of age have washed/  over this wrinkled body/ of mine 	pitifully/ awaiting another year’s end/ Suenomatsu Mountain

attributes.title: d24c37fa-6256-4c1e-9d71-f95d81725953
attributes.field_text: in my old home is/ one who vowed to wait for me/ Suenomatsu/ pines 	can it be that waves now/ rise and flood across her sleeves

attributes.title: 89dd5974-d60f-4725-908f-be15596c74e7
attributes.field_text: white waves seem to roll/ across Suenomatsu/ Mountain 	white caps seen/ as blossoms 	glowing beneath/ the bright moon of a spring night

attributes.title: 5ccbbb61-fae1-447e-9d9d-7417ee964b98
attributes.field_text: On the Nagara Bridge//  I came to see its/ decaying ruins 	that famous/ bridge of Nagara/ yet there’s only autumn wind/ blowing through the withered reeds

attributes.title: d37ef4b8-98ef-486a-bd2c-a67fa8342253
attributes.field_text: Viewing the reeds at the water’s edge in the province of Tsu//  surely I cannot/ linger in Nagara in/ the country of Tsu/ for this is a world where lives are/ short as the nodes of these reeds

attributes.title: bad82f0a-80da-4c94-ac85-0869f7635e00
attributes.field_text: On the Nagara Bridge//  as the years pass by/ the posts beneath the bridge grow/ ever more decayed/ only the name “as it was”/ is unchanged from days of old

attributes.title: 1c8067e4-f721-4b1c-bf8b-1af04c53cb0e
attributes.field_text: On the Nagara Bridge//  on a long spring day/ I tie my boat by the endless/ banks of Nagara/ River 	where might that bridge be/  I ask 	but no answer comes

attributes.title: b18e94e1-8c42-4f01-b483-5b4279cb731d
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.348
attributes.field_text: Hatsuse River/ there by those ancient waters/ towering two-trunked cedar/ after years have passed/ once more we’ll meet 	you and I/ towering two-trunked cedar

attributes.title: b07499a6-5745-47ee-b0e1-868aa56d919f
attributes.field_text: You mountain wind-blasts/ blowing from Hase Temple:/ in my prayer I asked/ for you to sway her my way  ̶   / not to make her rebuffs more harsh.

attributes.title: 5b79fc0f-2ced-4fef-9465-c33f87f4ab51
attributes.field_text: crossing Hatsuse/ Mountain as evening darkens/ seeking some shelter/ on the cypress-dotted fields/ of Miwa 	autumn winds blow

attributes.title: 4842bd45-88a2-4e42-b6d4-0787cbc6bd73
attributes.field_text: this welcome coolness/ can it mean autumn has returned/ Hatsuse River/ deep shade cast by cedars on/ the banks by ancient waters

attributes.title: 7baaa66d-4e7f-4505-a132-df1589817d05
attributes.field_text: hastening over/  the rocks 	Hatsuse River/ waves murmuring by my/ pillow flow 	swiftly 	this year/ has swept onward to its end

attributes.title: 0b7cd58b-2c32-4dd2-a5d1-970397ea7f44
attributes.field_text: in the fading blooms/ on Hatsuse Mountain 	spring/ draws to a close 	yet/ lingering on the peaks are/ the clouds we thought were flowers

attributes.title: 8dca7be5-8f18-40e3-911a-e0ff646636c1
attributes.field_text: as the years passed by/ my prayers for your vow of/  love died 	on the peak/  of Hatsuse the bell tolls 	now/ evening belongs to others

attributes.title: 8958742c-7096-4f75-aa15-1d04ac7cd68e
attributes.field_text: the deep sorrow of/ parting from someone who is/ a stranger to you  ̶   / passengers on a vessel/ leaving Matsura’s offing

attributes.title: 3a72fa78-b3c9-45f0-9505-c7af74a06136
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.164
attributes.field_text: I gaze across the/ endless plains of the sky 	can/ that moon be the one/ that comes from the rim of Mount/ Mikasa in Kasuga

attributes.title: 585a044d-28a9-4ffa-82b5-689a71db5ca1
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.348
attributes.field_text: broad as my lord’s 	an/ umbrella of clouds stretches/ above Mikasa Mountain/ the brilliant autumn/ leaves have been dyed in harvest/ colors by the early winter drizzle

attributes.title: b3840c99-1ac2-43f0-aa0e-410a6466f1e0
attributes.field_text: The Mount of Mikasa/ Is very far from you,/ I’d heard;/ Surely, not in such rain,/ Or so I did think!

attributes.title: e14c28ff-9c2f-49da-abba-64db2b27f929
attributes.field_text: Onto Mikasa mountain/ Drips the moon/ So clear that/ The god’s own heart/ Is clear, I think.

attributes.title: e8227428-ee56-4e33-83dc-0fd229e830ac
attributes.field_text: On Mount Mikasa/ Indeed, by the shade/ I am concealed, yet/ Continuing on seems pointless/ Under such a rain.

attributes.title: 9931fc74-fd38-4eb0-b538-dea7922ace21
attributes.field_text: why is it that those/  white clouds make their way up to/ Mikasa’s peak when/ They could tarry here in/  The foothills of the mountains

attributes.title: 6297b0ea-b2f5-4cf8-805e-6090bd32675a
attributes.field_text: under rainy skies/ aside from the shelter of/  Umbrella Mountain/ no protection do I/ receive 	do you not know this

attributes.title: abc43fa9-6f0b-4454-906b-dfa0a7cf5852
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.284
attributes.field_text: on Musashi Moor/ where autumn winds whistle in/ cold unending blasts/ no blade of grass is spared  ̶  / the color of each transformed

attributes.title: 8ecc986e-269e-499e-a37e-acc74d431f16
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.298
attributes.field_text: a single stalk of/ royal purple upon the/ Moor of Musashi/ makes me love all the other/ wild grasses all the more

attributes.title: b5f6bdf7-33db-4fe6-b062-8fefa3feb9db
attributes.field_text: Musashino field/ In autumn, with the scent of/  Patrinia blooms/ More so than at other times/  Longing for it consumes me!

attributes.title: 9dc2ff30-6654-4aee-8354-52e804d4bbb2
attributes.field_text: ah 	Musashi Moor/ no matter how far I go/ there is no end to/ autumn 	what wind is it that/ blows tips of distant grasses

attributes.title: 9b3c7ae7-4026-4c3d-8284-ed9f2e891853
attributes.field_text: my destination/ and the sky become one on/ Musashi Moor/ where from distant field grasses/  there emerges bright moonlight

attributes.title: e48a2818-585d-4d28-abbd-672da5af7ad1
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.372
attributes.field_text: as the rice boats ply/ the Mogami River 	they/ pole upstream and back  ̶   / you too should come again 	it’s/ only this month I say “no”

attributes.title: f2066e62-e541-4c3f-a0e9-949051f9a3df
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.154
attributes.field_text: oh barrier of / Ōsaka 	if restraint/ indeed you are 	hold/ back that one who wishes to/ leave before farewells are done

attributes.title: 8aece3ac-64c0-4a22-9969-023d8a503bc5
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.159
attributes.field_text: while still he crosses/ over and journeys onward/ leaving me behind/ your title 	Ōsaka/ Meeting Hill 	is just a name

attributes.title: c189dfb7-f2ce-4a8c-9b14-98ccd0034a47
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.184
attributes.field_text: I hear rumors of/ her 	borne by Mount Sound of Wings/ and yet here on the/  far side of Meeting Hill I/ pass the years in barren dreams

attributes.title: 62c7886f-523e-4216-8ac1-4fe5da1461f4
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.202
attributes.field_text: does the beribboned/ cock of Meeting Hill share my/ unfulfilled longings  ̶ / is it for love alone that/ we raise our solemn voices

attributes.title: e578a7d0-f87c-4780-93af-cd5bc677dd7e
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.203
attributes.field_text: the fresh spring waters/ surge freely through the rocky/ crevices of the/ Barrier at Meeting Hill 	but/ My words of love remain checked

attributes.title: 83cf33ad-7a13-492d-887d-3f7af892b289
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.231
attributes.field_text: I have yearned so long/ and at last tonight we meet  ̶ / may the beribboned/ cock at Ōsaka never/ announce the break of day

attributes.title: 013eebbb-c152-48e9-9ee5-1f0cccf1f158
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.261-262
attributes.field_text: oh if I could be/ the beribboned cock of the/ Ōsaka Road 	how/ plaintively I would cry out/ as I watched you come and go

attributes.title: a3dafd70-898e-4306-8bb2-29947fcf3e81
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.333
attributes.field_text: in Ōsaka/ the howling tempests rage and/  winds lash cold 	but still/ I know no place to go 	so/  I’ll sleep here in misery

attributes.title: 64cf1556-af83-4118-b47e-3c28fd485623
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.376-377
attributes.field_text: my passion shall stay/ hidden as the unopened/ buds of plume grasses/  on the Ōsaka slopes/ where I met my beloved

attributes.title: 60b30c12-5ae7-417a-b58a-41734e24669d
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.47
attributes.field_text: […] on yearning for one’s wife when one sees […] the grasses of summer, on offering prayer stripes on Ōsaka Hill, […]

attributes.title: 16461b21-ee48-4ff0-9ca0-12e08d4895cf
attributes.field_text: Sent out on my thoughts/  My heart is always able/ To pass through it, but/  The gate of the Meeting Slope/  It seems that I can’t get through.

attributes.title: c148b2cb-803e-42aa-a28a-c46f76e26703
attributes.field_text: Here it is: the gate/ where people coming and going/  must part company,/ where both friends and strangers meet  ̶ / on the slopes of Meeting Hill.

attributes.title: 9eff60e7-0dec-421a-8289-a7dee69f7da2
attributes.field_text: Through the night/ sodden from my travail/  the Chinese robe/   at Osaka Mountain/   I have lost my way.

attributes.title: f846062b-6978-42cd-b34d-a4ae2017dfaf
attributes.field_text: If true to their name,/ these “secret vines” I send you/ from Meeting Hill/ may wind me a way to you/  unseen by the eyes of men.

attributes.title: 8d48bd46-4893-4953-bd3f-f7ee6c5e9778
attributes.field_text: Meeting Hill lies/ Upon the road to the East/ I had heard, and yet/ My heart is exhausted by/ The barrier here!

attributes.title: f45a963c-610f-4d8a-bdb3-c74c98a5ac07
attributes.field_text: Has the spring at last crossed Ausaku barrier? The Otowa mountains are all in haze this morning?

attributes.title: 6f0c70db-8ab7-4beb-bcee-8240563ca0f4
attributes.field_text: Not a moment past/ Ausaka Barrier,/ When the feeling comes  ̶ / Already longing this morning/ For someone in the capital!

attributes.title: 02ce35f1-49ef-492b-b83c-c66733106ab0
attributes.field_text: Although it is known as the barrier of Ausaka, it still cannot retain the waters of Hashiri spring

attributes.title: 82b81aba-3d92-4f4c-818e-68044f4ef604
attributes.field_text: Try if you wish/  to fool others with rooster calls/ in the depths of night  ̶ / but still closed to your passage/ will be the gate at Meeting Hill.

attributes.title: d9f1ff63-32cb-42a7-958c-b627b47b1e5d
attributes.field_text: The dawntime/ Moon, too, in the waters clear/ Does lodge;/ This night I will not pass/ The Barrier at Meeting Hill.

attributes.title: 6ba4f555-7922-4eb4-9bd3-d8bec5c17bdd
attributes.field_text: a mountain thrush calls/ but still the snow flakes fall on/ cryptomeria/ needles 	silvery white/  mountains of Ōsaka

attributes.title: da42fdd9-a6b3-45fb-b60a-76985d14c36e
attributes.field_text: at Meeting Hill 	wind/ whistles through blossoms on slender/ branches 	as the storm/ grows 	it casts a haze over/ cedar groves at the barrier

attributes.title: db8eea19-9c16-4f2c-a695-8c7c11c8a364
attributes.field_text: were my home not near/ the Ōsaka barrier/ gate 	Meeting Hill 	then/ I’d not hope to meet again/ one who must now depart

attributes.title: 71b92b93-98c0-4b1f-8309-3395dd8ff507
attributes.field_text: rather than give up/ and wait for the approaching/  fresh year to bring you/  to me 	I will myself cross/ the Meeting Hill barrier

attributes.title: a47d45a8-a7e0-4786-9a99-04d9e83462f5
attributes.field_text: from this morning on/ I’ll kindle the fires of love/ ever more 	felling/ and stacking logs of heartache/ on the slopes of Meeting Hill

attributes.title: f410af67-e691-401b-8108-7623bdcd510c
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.83
attributes.field_text: the blowing winds which/ toss the mountain roses to/ the banks of River/ Yoshino 	have scattered their/ bright reflection in the depths

attributes.title: db211768-2a0a-4eaa-af41-0f27bcffa95a
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.183-184
attributes.field_text: so suddenly was/ my heart dyed with passion for/ you 	it leapt high as/ the waves in the waters of/ the swift Yoshino River

attributes.title: 401a8528-8400-46a0-a0d4-7fdc08bc2d22
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.190
attributes.field_text: the gurgling waters/ of the Yoshino River/ cut deep through the rocks  ̶  /in silence I will love you/ although I may die yearning

attributes.title: 3a5a8e3d-e122-44d3-94d6-d3d2080c6aef
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.236
attributes.field_text: Yoshino River/ the heart of the waters flows/ swiftly 	but I will/ never let rumors rise 	loud/ as the sound of the rapids

attributes.title: 6c8cfd24-4fdf-432e-8a92-0774427b026a
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.242
attributes.field_text: our meeting was as/ short as the thread between the/  gems of a necklace/ but the gossip will swell like/ the Yoshino River waves

attributes.title: 828fd688-c5f9-4add-8be6-952b922b78a6
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.250
attributes.field_text: like the waving sprays/ of wisteria boughs near/ the swift river at/ fair Yoshino 	my love flows/ to you in no common way

attributes.title: e1a3be5a-7e0f-41b0-be86-159ef9764962
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.277
attributes.field_text: although you’ve become/ cold as the waters of the/  Yoshino River/ I shall never forget the/ pledge I made when first we met

attributes.title: 14054d45-3948-43ec-82c2-f8b33baf4b43
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.286
attributes.field_text: like the Yoshino/ River cascading between/ Husband and Wife peaks/ obstacles forever part/ lovers in this world of ours

attributes.title: 8f623acd-24d8-4446-889d-012a7c3c0e7a
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.41
attributes.field_text: […] alluding to the Yoshino River, he complained of the ways of the world of love; […]

attributes.title: 07b80c10-fcc9-4cb0-9799-5d6be4709d95
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.142
attributes.field_text: in the first light of/ dawn it seems a reflection/ of the moon lingering/ above 	white snow has fallen/ here in Yoshino Village

attributes.title: ddbaba5b-5300-4b87-badc-f9627f4979ca
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.172
attributes.field_text: these bubbles of pearl/ foaming on the rapids of/ lovely Yoshino  ̶  / did men of old too 	see these/ as fragile gems 	here and gone

attributes.title: df99221d-7539-43b7-a9f1-ceff64c56b7e
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.50
attributes.field_text: where is it that the/ warm mists of spring are rising  ̶  / here on the slopes/  of lovely Mount Yoshino/ the snows continue to fall

attributes.title: f3777131-aede-499b-9cb6-53abc44cac04
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.66
attributes.field_text: far in the distance/ on lovely Mount Yoshino/ cherry blossoms must/ have opened 	for as I gazed/ I thought I saw snowdrifts there

attributes.title: eab1001d-c362-40ea-b889-bb74c10ed2df
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.138
attributes.field_text: as evening deepens/ the sleeves of my robe grow cold  ̶   / in fair Yoshino/ on lovely Mount Yoshino/ soft white snow must be falling

attributes.title: 9dca46f9-d62b-4357-90de-de4e047b6fbf
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.139
attributes.field_text: here in the ancient/ capital 	 Mount Yoshino/ is so near that not/ a single day passes when/ the dazzling snow does not fall

attributes.title: 54e7e7b0-44ad-480f-9d24-bf7d036493da
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.140
attributes.field_text: the white snows must be/ piling thickly on lovely/ Yoshino Mountain/ for in the old capital/ a bitter cold penetrates

attributes.title: 841b3d4a-ef67-43d5-9637-cba9b47c3b74
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.140
attributes.field_text: the one who trod this/ path through the untouched snows of/  fair Mount Yoshino/ sent not a word of greeting/ before leaving in silence

attributes.title: c231650c-631a-41b5-ab11-df016a8e0109
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.151
attributes.field_text: when upon lovely/ Mount Yoshino 	the heavy/  white snows swirl to earth/ the wind scatters the melting/ petals down to the foothills

attributes.title: 1d4ca4e3-49f9-48c1-b447-a7ec690a35ac
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.217-218
attributes.field_text: cherry blossoms of/  lovely Yoshino Mountain/ will be known to me/ only through the words of others  ̶   /until I too can go there

attributes.title: 4ae624dc-97e6-4d8f-893e-fbf0d6bb1aed
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.322
attributes.field_text: if only I had/ a home on the far side of/ fair Mount Yoshino/ I would make it my refuge/ In times of worldly sorrow

attributes.title: ac778341-c6b8-4208-870a-0cf7e8ad5c9d
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.322
attributes.field_text: as I grow older/ afflictions alone increase  ̶ / I will walk onward/ treading the narrow pathways/ through the crags of Yoshino

attributes.title: c070ad2f-9f12-4cec-af5b-a789a16d25d2
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.359
attributes.field_text: although you retreat/ deep within the Yoshino/ Mountains 	distant as/ far Cathay 	I am not one/ who will be left behind here

attributes.title: 2e59e354-9885-4021-a374-0ddd339e8cca
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.42
attributes.field_text: […], and on a spring morning the cherry blossoms on Yoshino Mountain reminded Hitomaro of clouds.

attributes.title: a756c8af-fba8-47f0-9e50-c1c84e172391
attributes.field_text: The flowers’ full bloom/ Is still not over, and yet,/ Yoshino river/ They fade in its reflection,/ Yamabuki on the banks.

attributes.title: cd93ef63-d1be-4d46-bea0-4a461724018b
attributes.field_text: Yoshino Mountain/ On Yoshino Mountain/ The cherry blossoms/ As white clouds I confuse them/ Seeing them again and again.

attributes.title: 335aaf33-a7e7-4d46-a6df-2a7abce3643c
attributes.field_text: So completely/ Am I to be despised- / If ’tis true, then/ On the mount of Yoshino/ I’ll find a place and tell no one!

attributes.title: 0da008de-07eb-4268-98b7-3bad0bd796bd
attributes.field_text: In fair Yoshino/ Sealed in by snow,/ A mountain man:/ Searching out paths past,/ I wonder does he, too, weep aloud?

attributes.title: 7d2c374b-a172-446b-b1de-e6facbd88f45
attributes.field_text: Is it only because/ The calendar says spring has come?/ Even the mountains/  At Yoshino this morning/  Are faintly touched with haze.

attributes.title: 326d4764-0995-464b-8d55-1f94758abedd
attributes.field_text: The old capital/  Is given over to spring;/ At fair Yoshino/ The meadows of Mikaki/ Are covered over with mist.

attributes.title: dc2b9d0f-9a64-44c8-8a51-120295949b53
attributes.field_text: At fair Yoshino/ In the shade of Kisa mou[n]tain/ Stands a pine:/ How many Autumn winds/ Have brought you to this pass, I wonder.

attributes.title: 77eb0b01-6aa8-4814-b1a5-344b89f6ec2d
attributes.field_text: In fair Yoshino/ The blossoms’ bounty/ I see today, so/ In Koshi on Shirane peak/ The spring breezes will be blowing.

attributes.title: d354a9c6-8d3d-4ed4-a393-1fa7b520b2b4
attributes.field_text: I’ll see the blossoms/ parting grasses on ancient/ streets with each stride  ̶  / daybreak in springtime at/ palace ruins in Yoshino

attributes.title: d8e78ca1-50a5-46b2-b1df-2e786d9c613c
attributes.field_text: here in Yoshino/ on the Natsumi River/ floating in quiet/  eddies 	a duck is crying/ deep in the mountains’ shadow

attributes.title: ebca4925-050e-4cc5-90e9-11923e9cd6cd
attributes.field_text: renouncing the world/ to dwell in Yoshino’s depths/ sweet-voiced song bird/ can it be you truly know/ my heart’s deepest recesses

attributes.title: 82a29aa4-f94c-48df-a9aa-85d452fcb47a
attributes.field_text: at Mizunoe/ the palace of Yoshino/ is awe-inspiring/ ancient are the twisted pines/ howling in winds from the bay

attributes.title: 8ae7d869-4d48-429e-b69a-2e3755519b2b
attributes.field_text: despising the world/ I came here 	where I must hate/ it all the more 	deep/ in the mountains of Yoshino/ autumn evening gathers

attributes.title: a1a0ecba-9251-4773-93d4-ac87a35c2ee0
attributes.field_text: Yoshino River/ on its banks yellow mountain/ roses have opened/ surely the cherry blossoms/ of the peaks have all fallen

attributes.title: ba76b9c4-47c4-42e8-a83a-5c7e8f2bb9f6
attributes.field_text: Yoshino mountains/ snow flakes scattering on bare/ branches of cherry/ trees 	surely this is a year/ when the blossoms will come late

attributes.title: 1fe3bb0c-0862-44a6-94db-77a186adde36
attributes.field_text: The pathway I marked/ when last year I made my way/  into Yoshino  ̶  / I abandon now to visit/ blossoms I have not yet seen.

attributes.title: b0ebfa4f-a3b2-412e-b900-0b048d46cd1d
attributes.field_text: on Mount Yoshino/  the cherry blossoms must now/ be their most dazzling  ̶  / reluctant to leave their old/ home 	white clouds cling to the peak

attributes.title: cbeb83fe-eba6-4888-b0dd-fd7f4a463344
attributes.field_text: from so far away/ petals dancing as they fall  ̶  / splendors of Mount/  Yoshino 	are white clouds whirled in/ Tumult by the summit storms

attributes.title: f2a3124f-8fba-4bda-9737-52647b08aabb
attributes.field_text: At the old capital/ in the hills of Yoshino/ the blossoms are gone;/ it is through empty branches/ that spring breezes are blowing.

attributes.title: 761c2d63-aa74-46fc-a1c2-51dd7e1b3b0d
attributes.field_text: who watches tonight/ as wind 	blowing through slender/ bamboo pierces his/ body 	who gazes upon/ the moon on Yoshino’s Peak

attributes.title: 352812f1-a4f6-4c30-8685-03d5579bd4f7
attributes.field_text: now at long last I/ can view the fairest blooms/ of the mountains of/ Yoshino as garden flowers/ at my own new residence

attributes.title: 0e73edf2-7c94-4904-b684-b3fdcb7a8268
attributes.field_text: Here I am, thinking/ I may never again leave/ the Yoshino hills,/ while they think as they wait,/ “Surely once the blossoms fall…”

attributes.title: e00cc568-b99b-420b-b840-74373ea9ffa0
attributes.field_text: Flowers must be falling/  on Yoshino’s peaks:/ this spring dawn’s/ gusting winds/ blossom in white.

attributes.title: 0a4da852-0346-44e1-ab8b-ab09d757fd37
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.136
attributes.field_text: is autumn leaving/  with the belling voices of/  the deer 	now growing/ fainter on Mount Ogura/ as the twilight approaches

attributes.title: 84b98e48-017f-4e13-9658-dea816c8ccf9
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.174
attributes.field_text: wearing down the peak/ of Mount Ogura 	pacing/ loudly belling 		no/ one knows how many autumns/ this deer has cried for his love

attributes.title: 205aa7a3-028c-4bbe-981e-ece4b94c8860
attributes.field_text: Oh what shall I do!/ On dark Ogura Mountain/ The summer cuckoo/ Is crying out and saying/ “I can’t see to find my way!”

attributes.title: e56c1c23-829b-435e-9c7c-2c1e54d6c8fd
attributes.field_text: Spring is closing in/ And the falling white snow/ On Ogura Mountain/ On the peak there are flowers/  In the height of their bloom.

attributes.title: 2b5ee393-9ef5-43ea-b292-cd31d392e7a7
attributes.field_text: On the Ōi River/ Float boats with/ Fishing fires and/ Gloomy Mount Ogura/ Is so in name alone.

attributes.title: e4632fdc-7be6-4b1a-b25b-2e9bba411bd0
attributes.field_text: You autumn leaves/ on the slopes at Ogura  ̶  / if you have a heart,/ put off your falling this once:/ till the Emperor’s visit.

attributes.title: 21c640ba-368f-4b49-979d-eab917f338f0
attributes.field_text: Ogura Mountain/ at its foot flowering plume/ grass blankets the fields/  spearheads dimly visible/ this dusky autumn evening

attributes.title: c4500b4a-28a9-4977-96f9-01894411fae5
attributes.field_text: could there be a place/ where tonight’s brilliant moon is/ hidden behind clouds  ̶  / even dusky Ogura/ Mountain must find a new name

attributes.title: 14206f47-8479-4b4e-8757-41be05c76d93
attributes.field_text: the mournful cries of/ the wild geese are the only/  voices I hear on/ dark Ogura Mountain where/ the mists never lift or clear

attributes.title: 9bcb4f45-f092-4bac-8387-44f8ad112911
attributes.field_text: in this village in dark foothills of Ogura Mountain 	the trees have  lost their leaves 	in the tree tops I see the brightening moon

attributes.title: 06345d1c-1a12-4fd3-80c6-1f97efb84a82
attributes.field_text: I left the capital/ Together with the rising/ Mists of spring, but/ Autumn winds are blowing now/ At Shirakawa Barrier.

attributes.title: 63fc588a-e92b-4f77-8f90-7a1f357fc26a
attributes.field_text: In the capital,/ There still were leaves of green/ Upon which to turn my gaze, yet/ Scattered scarlet leaves cover/ The barrier at Shirakawa.

attributes.title: d8eb5f34-f8aa-41f2-9317-681f4e5d0106
attributes.field_text: Over and over/  To Ikuta Bay I have come/ And then gone back home/  The waves crashing over me/ Seem to have drenched thoroughly.

attributes.title: 101f659e-ced0-4c03-9941-7ba098b395ec
attributes.field_text: Coming and going/ It is the tide where in time/ The dampness will dry/  That is simply natural/  When you visit Ikuta Bay.

attributes.title: ee0f8625-e745-4300-906c-759534a796c0
attributes.field_text: even yesterday/ I though [sic] that I would visit/ and now autumn has/ come to Ikuta grove in/ the fabled province of Tsu

attributes.title: 1d6010bc-b4dd-4c28-84a2-27705ec2ae43
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.195
attributes.field_text: restlessly drifts my/ heart 	as unsettled as the/ bobbing buoys of the/  fisherfolk who cast their nets/ into the sea at Ise

attributes.title: 6cffc311-fbde-40e9-a27c-a8c729f3eb8c
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.195
attributes.field_text: as never-ending/ as the relentless tasks of/ fisherfolk who cast/ their nets and reel them in on/ Ise Sea 	love consumes me

attributes.title: d1d2ebe5-76a4-4e9a-b954-016af626b1ab
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.246
attributes.field_text: as fisherfolk of/ Ise dive for seaweed from/ morning until night  ̶   / oh that I might see you 	till/ my longing could be sated

attributes.title: 404fcce9-3a8e-40bd-9d1f-9e9afb7f427f
attributes.field_text: Could such a mediocre Fisherman harvest? I think not!/ The sea at Ise/ Sends waves high upon the shore/ Where the algae grows!

attributes.title: 437a4b52-eed1-4984-9f5f-388f3da707f9
attributes.field_text: By the sea at Ise/ A diver-girl does work/ Without surcease/ Endlessly/ I hate myself!

attributes.title: db08f130-79ad-4762-a926-5b234e673f3b
attributes.field_text: spreading out the reeds/ growing along Ise shore/ where the divine winds/ blow 	does he break his journey/ there 	sleeping on the rough beach

attributes.title: 5e6f8717-99d1-451c-ab97-d434707f62d4
attributes.field_text: how many nights have/  I gazed in astonishment/ at the moon 	here at/ Ise where waves break as I/ spread the reeds upon the shore

attributes.title: 502c3ae1-4463-4096-b3cc-861efe9b6df1
attributes.field_text: forging through the waves/ of a myriad rapids/ unfamiliar to/ me 	I sleep alone 	spreading/  the reeds of the Ise shore

attributes.title: a8c34318-2395-41b5-803e-55f79da34823
attributes.field_text: so cold 	the wind 	as/ I make my way through the reeds/ on the Ise shore  ̶  / borrowing a robe 	crying/ the geese fly above the waves

attributes.title: 336d9e7a-e78c-444d-80bf-d2929843b9ae
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.247
attributes.field_text: tonight once again/ does she spread but one side of/ her robe upon the/ mat 	bridge maiden of Uji/  do your arms still await me

attributes.title: ecac87a3-81e5-4fcb-8707-2fa714479702
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.285
attributes.field_text: forgotten 	forlorn/ am I 	for our love crumbled/ like the Uji Bridge  ̶   / this whole year long 	there has been/ no traffic across the gulf

attributes.title: 6e23136a-63b8-48f2-a9bf-a8447443e528
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.309
attributes.field_text: oh once vigorous/ guardian of Uji Bridge/ which I’ve so often/ crossed 	how pitiful to see/ you bent with the passing years

attributes.title: 436fb8f3-5507-46af-911f-9569758ef554
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.332
attributes.field_text: this is how I live/ in my retreat southeast of/ the capital 	though/ men call Uji Mountain a/ reminder of worldly sorrow

attributes.title: b251c9be-ac1f-42c2-9bea-3b8948c9d596
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.45
attributes.field_text: This is how I live/ in my retreat southwest of/  the capital 	though/ men call Uji Mountain a/  reminder of wordly [sic] sorrow

attributes.title: 0643b52e-f84f-44e0-a696-6b0153707cca
attributes.field_text: If I didn’t see/ Autumn leaves from Mount Uji/ I would not know that/ The days of the long month/ Had passed by like the hio.

attributes.title: 6edee61e-72b9-4d12-9551-134034389867
attributes.field_text: In morning’s first light/ the mists on Uji River/ are all breaks and gaps  ̶   / and appearing everywhere,/ bamboo stakes of fishing weirs.

attributes.title: cba4aa76-be5e-43a4-a749-f29d8e237abd
attributes.field_text: Toward what harbor/ spring goes when it fades away/ one cannot know  ̶  / a barge of firewood falling/ into River Uji’s haze.

attributes.title: 36707336-1ea3-4037-a409-ff5a9340c30c
attributes.field_text: foothills enveloped/ by the mists rising above/ the Uji River/ while 	in the cloud-seat 	morning/  sunlight strikes Mount Akashi

attributes.title: f8396c4b-80c1-487e-b9a2-0b61d48c544c
attributes.field_text: on her thin straw mat/  robe half-spread to sleep alone/ maiden at the bridge/  awaiting the empty night/  in vain 	daybreak at Uji

attributes.title: f5be6f42-508b-4fc0-809a-31152b958ae0
attributes.field_text: was this happiness/ enfolded in her single/  sleeve 	spread as she slept  ̶  / the long-awaited day has come/ maiden of the Uji bridge

attributes.title: 3ff1575b-d36a-4fa4-b26d-f0f9fcbe98bb
attributes.field_text: oh 	guardian of/ the all-powerful Uji/ bridge I’ve so of the/  crossed 	how pitiful to see/ you bent with the passing years

attributes.title: 51332801-3aba-4f83-91a8-4a5d78c591d1
attributes.field_text: cormorant fishing/ boats 	how they tug at my heart/ myriad warriors/  of Uji River 	lights flicker/ under the evening sky

attributes.title: 3f8e0d1c-a172-4a53-af61-b35e16638437
attributes.field_text: although there have been/ times when my heart leapt like/ rapids on Uji/ River 	there has also been/ heartache that our clan might end

attributes.title: 2c054a9a-cc3d-46e0-9c7b-28ff24ae65ba
attributes.field_text: like waves wandering/ through the pilings of the weir/ in Uji 	river/ of the eighty warrior/ clans 	I know not where I go

attributes.title: a5a59720-b51b-4dc2-8da0-d9ac6cd5febf
attributes.field_text: On a mat of rush/ as autumn winds deepen/ her night of waiting,/  the Maiden of Uji Bridge/ spreads a robe of moonlight.

attributes.title: ffad5a62-4a6a-48a8-a0e5-0d62f9878413
attributes.field_text: On the Ōi River/ Float boats with/ Fishing fires and/ Gloomy Mount Ogura/ Is so in name alone.

attributes.title: 0d8eb83d-17e6-4033-a577-93e9df56da5e
attributes.field_text: At Ōigawa:/ O, pine trees on the bank/ I would ask you something:/ Was there ever such an imperial visit/ In the days of long ago?

attributes.title: 00fb73b0-0631-482c-af10-b121dae6f4a0
attributes.field_text: From upstream/ Flow the scarlet leaves upon/ The River Ōi/ Seeming to spatter colour on/ The cataracts’ white threads…

attributes.title: 1bda7dda-64c3-4a40-84f5-70d039a96344
attributes.field_text: No water/ To be seen around at/ The River Ōi/ Yet on the banks the scarlet leave/ Do fall as rain…

attributes.title: 7b618b55-c541-444f-8f05-68b38e7c436b
attributes.field_text: Fallen in piles are/ The scarlet leaves – when I see them at/ The River Ōi/ The weirs and dams autumn/ Have held in place…

attributes.title: cc3b5aa3-146e-4c7f-b832-15d580e67037
attributes.field_text: The River Ōi:/ This ancient flow/ Have I come to visit, and/ Around the mount of storms,/ Scarlet leaves I see!

attributes.title: 9a8196e3-a6a1-4cce-aef6-8a5260c38018
attributes.field_text: how many rapids/ will they have crossed 	cormorant/ fishing boats on Ōi/ River 	poling by with lanterns/ lit till the summer night dawns

attributes.title: 714352f4-a6b0-444c-a56b-fb8656e40bdb
attributes.field_text: fallen and scattered/ autumn leaves cannot float past/  on Ōi River/ where is the palisade that/ obstructs these swirling waters

attributes.title: 88f64498-78c5-41c5-b30b-dc09f8728d2c
attributes.field_text: shallow drafted boats/ struggle slowly on 	so thickly/ do the autumn leaves/ come flowing with the waters/ of the Ōi River

attributes.title: 30780e69-e97c-4c26-a6a9-9e68e7f694d5
attributes.field_text: Ōi River/ waters swell within the sluice  ̶   / for was not today/ the day you promised to meet/ in a rare tryst at nightfall

attributes.title: 40e0357d-e907-4879-b437-9910d5fe4172
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.149-150
attributes.field_text: veils of mist must be/ rising now over Saho/ River where plovers/ cry 	here on the mountainside/ the colors of the leaves deepen.

attributes.title: de1cd534-c409-41e0-8579-08250a552c68
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.124
attributes.field_text: oh mists of autumn/ please 	just this one morning  	let/ me see from afar/ the brilliant autumn-tinged leaves/ of the oaks on Mount Saho

attributes.title: 3a40e1ad-bbc1-484e-a1dd-dc415e24de39
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.124
attributes.field_text: although the colors/ of the oaks on Mount Saho/ are still shallow and/ faint 	already we have reached/ the mournful depths of autumn

attributes.field_text: the deep red oak leaves/ of Saho Mountain will soon/ fall 	even at night/ the moonlight gleams brightly to/ display their autumn beauty

attributes.title: cbd79414-7587-492b-a140-a0086ae20b16
attributes.field_text: When winter arrives/  At the banks of Saho river/ The sitting crane/ Has trouble sleeping alone/ I hear crying in pain.

attributes.title: 4cd0d12f-3312-4692-929c-98e57732d21e
attributes.field_text: In heaven’s river/ They geese cry and cross the gate/ Oh, now I see why/ Branches on Saho Mountain/ Are tinged with autumn color.

attributes.title: 404c2971-f304-47aa-862a-8cacb8dab1f9
attributes.field_text: The first late year rain/ Has barely started to fall/ When on Mt. Saho/ Every branch of all the trees/ Have already changed color.

attributes.title: 2e4e4850-a08e-4405-8166-29d8dd3c24e3
attributes.field_text: The River Sao:/ Mist rises, and from beyond/ Come plover cries,/ Their calls uninterrupted/ By anything.

attributes.title: 6a367e36-52b4-468c-90a0-09abb8d5b763
attributes.field_text: night is falling on/ the road I must travel 	and/ yet 	how wrenching it/ is to leave behind Saho/ River where the plovers cry

attributes.title: bd240649-9c45-4efa-83c5-18b4f40533e3
attributes.field_text: though my source is in/ the Saho River which has/ flowed for many years/ alas 	I have run into/ hazardous currents and sunk

attributes.field_text: is the heart of this/  god we celebrate today/ swayed by our appeals/ prayer strips ripple like wind/ tossed waves on Saho River

attributes.field_text: As the setting sun/ shines on the groves of great oaks/ on Sao Mountain,/ a cloudless sky is raining  ̶   / as the leaves keep on falling.

attributes.field_text: in this Godless Month/ chilly rains must be falling/ for on Mount Saho/ the winter creeper’s verdant/ color deepens steadily

attributes.field_text: seeing the shadows/  cast by Ogura Mountain/ where dusk is constant/ visitors 	thinking the sun/ has set 		now hurry away

attributes.field_text: the mists spread over/ the Abukuma 	but though/ dawn has come 	I will/ not send him away 	for to/ have to wait is too painful

attributes.title: 134d6d53-2e84-42a9-954a-0f0e52c30ced
attributes.field_text: As long as the world lasts/ The Abukuma River/ Is very far,/ So your image in the deeps/  Not seeing it, I suffer.

attributes.field_text: at your journey’s end/ Abukuma River 	if/ there were no hope of/ our meeting again 	what would/ we feel at today’s parting

attributes.field_text: I know you await/ our hoped-for meeting 	River/ of Abukuma/ yet I’m saddened by the thought/ of the few years left to me

attributes.title: ca194ed6-a81f-4323-9df6-f50174fd99dd
attributes.field_text: living in the reign/ of my lord 	even submerged/ logs beneath the ice/ of Abukuma River/ anticipate the spring thaw

attributes.title: cb47055b-987c-4530-a5e4-917d39e09a24
attributes.field_text: Near Arima Hill/ the wind through Ina’s bamboos/ blows constantly  ̶  / and just as constant am I/ in my resolve not to forget.

attributes.title: ba3af56c-91bb-455a-9505-2c2f919ec61d
attributes.field_text: traveling across/ Ina plain  	where the grebes flock  ̶  / on Mount Arima/ the evening mists are rising/ but I have no place to rest

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.265
attributes.field_text: had I merely dreamt/ and never crossed those sounding/ waves of Otowa/ River 	I would never have/ known the chill waters of love

attributes.title: 7773c5af-70a6-4f00-801a-9d538a8c9dc7
attributes.field_text: At the cataracts on Otowa river where water is pouring down the weir, is it possible to have a glimpse of his heart?

attributes.field_text: only rumors tell/ me that my dear one is there/ Otowa River/ if I cross over 	I’ll see/ her reflection in my sleeves

attributes.field_text: clearly I can see/ that your heart is not shallow/ though these are not those/  waters of Otoha River/ damned up to rush this way

attributes.field_text: shall my love be known/ to all by the prattling of/ gossip 	whispering/ echoing like Sound of Wings/ Rapids in Yamashina

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.184
attributes.field_text: I hear rumors of/ her 	borne by Mount Sound of/ Wings/ and yet here on the/  far side of Meeting Hill I/ pass the years in barren dreams

attributes.title: 748edcd4-e82c-489a-9fe9-777136139e93
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.240
attributes.field_text: would I reveal our/ love 	would I give gossip wings/ send it whispering/ echoing 	like Sound of Wings/ Mountain in Yamashina

attributes.title: 464d04f2-a44c-44b0-bcda-f86c24a38db5
attributes.field_text: I have only heard/ Rumors of the cuckoo at/  Otoha mountain/ I hear it and I hear it/ But I can’t meet it at all.

attributes.title: 62a3fdd4-e2bc-4c24-9eb9-ee19e387094b
attributes.field_text: The autumn wind which/  Which [sic] invites the first crying/  Of the bell crickets/  From the Otoha Mountain/ It seems to begin to blow.

attributes.title: 4586e528-cca9-4281-a15a-54a33ed8692c
attributes.field_text: the autumn wind comes/ whistling from all directions/ Otowa Mountain/ which of the grasses and trees/ can accept it tranquilly

attributes.title: 0e440241-cc37-48ee-bf51-ea46138f149f
attributes.field_text: Otowa Mountain/ the white snow gleams so clearly/ so brightly 	that now/ the sound of the cock crowing/ reports the breaking dawn

attributes.title: ab315caf-7c47-40c8-b092-27c7b3573fce
attributes.field_text: Mother is away/ past Ōe and Ikuno,/ near Heaven’s Ladder,/ whence would come her letter  ̶  / but neither have I yet seen.

attributes.title: e2adcf2b-1059-4c17-8084-18b33471ffcd
attributes.field_text: crossing Ōe/ Mountain 	traveling toward/ the distant end of/ Ikuno road 	lucky to/ be on the Way in this world

attributes.title: ffa698fc-e00e-4ceb-b372-afd01645f628
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.299
attributes.field_text: Oshio Mountain/ in Ōhara 	today/ especially 	must/ call to mind the events of/ the age of the awesome gods

attributes.title: 9b6741ea-c3fa-4254-9ac6-b3c8579a428e
attributes.field_text: At Ōhara,/ On Oshio Mountain/ The young pine saplings/ Will grow swiftly into mighty trees and/ See a thousand generations pass!

attributes.title: 1b0d6158-9788-4529-b94f-ff874e3d640e
attributes.field_text: I came here hoping/ to turn my back on the world’s/ sorrows 	but I have/ found even more misery/ in the village of Ōhara

attributes.title: affc389e-c6d3-4faa-ab96-c7aa79cbe94a
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.181
attributes.field_text: autumn has come 	and/ although the laurel tree of/ the moon bears no fruit/ it scatters shimmering beams/ of light like falling petals

attributes.title: 15817c02-d137-443a-823a-6a19069440c7
attributes.field_text: The only reason/ We went out the other time/ To see Katsura House/ Was to make it logical/  We should view Moon Disk today.

attributes.title: 39b0ce62-32aa-4af4-9f30-63d706535a0a
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.188
attributes.field_text: as priests behind their sleeves/ with mulberry strands to pray/ to the mighty gods/ at Kamo Shrine 	my heart is/ bound by thoughts of you each day

attributes.title: 88f5c6aa-ffba-4c24-8ca8-2f8770b28c03
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.374
attributes.field_text: cherished pines before/ the shrine of the awesome gods/ at Kamo 	surely/  their color will never change/ though ten thousand years may pass

attributes.title: 99b398f1-86ab-4958-920e-b29801c417ad
attributes.field_text: At Kamo River/ The moon’s reflection is clear/ On the river’s depths,/ Maybe that’s why people come/ For the purification.

attributes.title: e2b7eb2f-ae6e-4ddb-a09a-6917d2ed6365
attributes.field_text: With this simply/ Should it end?/ Puissant/ Kamo Shrine/ Will see ten thousand ages pass!

attributes.title: e95df49b-f80b-47b3-bf42-334c8859f693
attributes.field_text: Puissant/ Kamo’s river shore by/ Wisteria waves is/ Washed; forgotten/ Never will you be!

attributes.title: af1ce4eb-5393-4fc9-ae69-9e98bf0c3c56
attributes.field_text: Puissant/ Kamo Shrine’s/ Deity, hear me!/ If my love forsakes me not,/ Then never will I forsake him!

attributes.title: df1da8e3-3fa9-4797-a8f7-63d38a24bbf2
attributes.field_text: Whatever/ The heart desires within/ The dread/ And ancient/ Walls of Kamo.

attributes.title: 4da8b85f-954f-421f-afd2-0a05f26c0cbf
attributes.field_text: withered heartvine 	how/ sad that we have grown apart/ do you not see it/ so 	waters flow swiftly past/ that holy fence at Kamo

attributes.title: 5efc7152-9a25-4db1-b92b-52a5f4ad1fe9
attributes.field_text: His Majesty, Saga’s mountain/ Excursion is long done, yet/ By the river Seri/ For a thousand generations will the ancient ways/ Leave their mark.

attributes.title: 223b110a-d839-4d97-b9e0-ffbb3102fa8d
attributes.field_text: Should I still be here/ Till autumn when the young bush clover/ Will be in flower,/ I’ll remember this was the day/ They burned Saga moor in spring

attributes.title: be9f3a3e-6487-4d16-87c4-1d98b1037f6c
attributes.field_text: even were matters/ not so 	a visit to dew drenched/ meadows of Saga/ would weigh down my flowing sleeves  ̶  / memories of days of old

attributes.title: 57adae2d-2dca-4c86-adbd-e360a589cc22
attributes.field_text: sadness is autumn’s/ way 	on Saga Meadow/ are the cicadas/ raising their cries ever more/ loudly 	in our old village

attributes.title: bf481646-5e17-4eba-a9ab-b41628e35ff3
attributes.field_text: now must I treasure/ these meadows of Saga as/ keepsakes of the dew/ that vanished in the fields 	such/ is the way of this sad world

attributes.title: 8520c849-b921-49e8-9212-7e4091a61363
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.257
attributes.field_text: like the twisted cloth/ colored in far Shinobu/ of the deep north 	if/ not for you 	for whom would I/ dye my heart with tangled love

attributes.title: 1623439a-9fa5-4077-85d1-262236dff060
attributes.field_text: You, alone/ To the estates of Shinobu/ Have gone;/ As Mount Abitsu /As far, it seems!

attributes.title: d02ce164-4d9a-4b99-8854-f8075c811bd7
attributes.field_text: days pass in longing/  for the capital 	storms rage/ over the waters/  of lonely Shinobu Bay/ no tiding but those of waves

attributes.title: c930bf93-749b-41b9-8f67-deeab4d871fd
attributes.field_text: endlessly reeling  ̶  / painful the gaze of strangers/ that I must endure  ̶  / fishermen of Shinobu Bay/ haul on mulberry ropes

attributes.title: 7698a6c4-9eb1-4160-85ff-704c4b3e22da
attributes.field_text: I cannot help but/ feel hatred for the cloudless/ night 	the brilliant moon/ of autumn illuminates my/ retreat 	Shinobu Village

attributes.title: b6b14052-8a01-4cb1-8162-d1420fcb776c
attributes.field_text: in Michinoku’s/ Iwade 	Shinobu 	if/  you yearn in silence/ none can know 	send a letter/ Tsubonoishibumi

attributes.title: 6944d198-9801-4863-8686-a2ea6b829980
attributes.field_text: surely the first cold/ rains of winter have not left/ these autumn leaves on/ Mt. Shinobu undyed just/ to urge the storms to rage on

attributes.title: e35e999f-1e31-4de1-9214-7168915e06ab
attributes.field_text: unbeknownst to her/ such misery I endure/ hidden like the backs/ of creeping arrowroot leaves/ beneath Shinobu Mountain

attributes.title: e2ff33b5-f105-404d-9ca8-c4668501da2a
attributes.field_text: let them disappear/ those clouds that are concealing/ Mount Shinobu’s peak/ until this yearning heart too is/ gone without a single trace

attributes.title: 0a24db61-b0fe-45c1-a510-613c45464cab
attributes.field_text: there is a limit to/ endurance 	in the foothills/ of Mount Shinobu/ even dew drops covering/ the fallen leaves change color

attributes.field_text: a covering of/ bright scattered leaves floats on the/ Tatsuta River  ̶  / were I to ford the waters/ the brocade would tear in half

attributes.field_text: the brilliant autumn/ leaves float by on Tatsuta/ River 	freezing rains/ must already be falling/ on holy Mount Mimuro

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.131
attributes.field_text: unheard of 	even/ in the stories of the age/ of the awesome gods  ̶  / the waters of Tatsuta/ Stream dyed with swirling red

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.133
attributes.field_text: because autumn is/ returning 	crossing over/ Kannabi Mountain/ she offers crimson prayer/ stripes at Tatsuta River

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.133
attributes.field_text: if no colored leaves/ drifted downstream there 	who would/ know that autumn had/  come to the clear waters/ of the Tatsuta River

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.135-136
attributes.field_text: seeing the color/ of the waters which tumble/ down the beautiful/ mountains 	I know full well that/ this autumn is at its end

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.136
attributes.field_text: every year the/ Tatsuta River carries/ the colored leaves past  ̶  / is it that the river mouth/ is the berth of autumn

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.137
attributes.field_text: on the Tatsuta/ River the Godless Month weaves/ a brocade of leaves/ red and gold upon the sharp/ silver warp and weft of sleet

attributes.title: c345d39e-1fa7-474b-a1bd-5bd3fde36597
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.230
attributes.field_text: already rumors/ swirl 	though as yet there is no/ truth to them 	can I/ now refrain from venturing/ forth to ford Tatsuta’s course

attributes.title: 37e82acb-5edd-4a35-86b4-d1d900764630
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.42
attributes.field_text: On an autumn evening the crimson leaves floating on the Tatsuta River looked like brocade to the sovereign, and on a spring morning the cherry blossoms on Yoshino Mountain reminded Hitomaro of clouds.

attributes.title: 92e330dc-71c3-454e-b5f0-3d4b081e0152
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.42
attributes.field_text: We have such examples as the Nara Mikado, Heizei’s, poem:  a covering of/  bright scattered leaves floats on the/  Tatsuta River  ̶  / were I to ford the waters/ the brocade would tear in half.  Hitomaro’s:  the plum blossoms now/ are indistinguishable  ̶  / for snow mists the broad/ heavens and masks all below/ in a whirling world of white

attributes.title: 2772eccb-c621-4b25-82bb-14fbeaa4a480
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.79
attributes.field_text: surely it is the/  falling of the blossoms that/  he mourns 	the mountain/ thrush cries on Mount Tatsuta/ where spring mists drift skyward

attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.335
attributes.field_text: as the howling winds/ keep white waves rising in the/ offing 	in the deep/ of night 	is my lord crossing/ Tatsuta Mountain alone
