attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.336
attributes.field_text: whose cock 	adorned with/ purification ribbons/ crows incessantly/ on bright Tatsuta Mountain/ colorful as Chinese robes

attributes.title: e1060eb3-c6c0-42f2-9eef-33de2576ced1
attributes.field_text: The Tatsuta River/ I see has now changed into/ A scarlet color./ Apparently the mountain’s/ Autumn leaves have now fallen.

attributes.title: 0fc3bcef-5e13-4707-98db-b773eb81d809
attributes.field_text: Tatsuta River/ When autumn season arrives/ Is close to mountains,/ So the flowing water, too,/ Changes color as the leaves.

attributes.title: 01fb7561-caad-4f44-a308-cdd7e08d0b1d
attributes.field_text: Tatsuta river:/ How I whish that in autumn,/ The water would dry!/ I don’t want to see the leaves/ Float away from my vision.

attributes.title: 08097dbe-3915-4061-b069-b486c4927a7d
attributes.field_text: As soon as the geese/ Cry on their return, just then,/ The Chinese clothing/ Tatsuta mountain is filled/ With the colored autumn leaves.

attributes.title: 119e5e72-a14d-4e89-91b5-75888a769dbd
attributes.field_text: My lover’s robe cord/ Tied to release I set off/ On Mount Tatsuya/ Now the colored autumn leaves/ Have been woven as brocade.

attributes.title: 397ff8ec-31e5-4af0-b89d-e6ef6a1e7ca4
attributes.field_text: The geese are crying/ In the cold of the morning/ It seems there is dew/ Thus on Tatsuta Mountain/ The leaves are starting to change.

attributes.title: d3f0fbe4-fb00-40b9-ad70-354e02773d8c
attributes.field_text: The coloring of/ The autumn leaves is so deep/ Perhaps that is why/ This mountain was given the name/ Brocade making Tatsuta.

attributes.title: be989735-c26b-40c5-ade0-7fec557e018f
attributes.field_text: Of Chinese brocade/ Even Tatsuta Mountain/ If only, from now,/ The leaves could remain colored/ And stay for eternity.

attributes.title: 16e12a76-7756-43d7-9135-590dba9855ab
attributes.field_text: Of Chinese clothing/ On Tatsuta Mountain/ The Leaves of autumn/ Though not woven with a loom/ The leaves are still a brocade.

attributes.title: 8aeb2d53-cc4b-43fc-b299-3764ee5d3a5e
attributes.field_text: Why ask, even now/ Whether this is now autumn?/ This is a world where/ Tatsuta Mountain is draped/ In a colored leaf brocade.

attributes.title: af4e14a6-d6e8-4b40-9bc5-d9d4f955732e
attributes.field_text: They should be now accustomed, that in summer clothes we come again and again to the shades of the willows in the riverbed of Tatsuta river

attributes.title: 1d674785-d0d2-4753-a117-1a372c73566b
attributes.field_text: The winds of a storm/ blowing on Mount Mimuro/ have brought autumn leaves/ down to Tatsuta River  ̶  / and made it a rich brocade.

attributes.title: bb96a91a-2029-4d94-b9bf-2cf08520c4c2
attributes.field_text: From spring yearning for the first blossoms hidden in the mists rising on Mt. Tatsuta, the summer mountain nightingale of the sacred mountains yearning for his mate, autumn’s bright colored leaves on Kazuraki falling in the wind, to the end of the year in winter when snow piles up like white linen on the towering peak of Fuji, each poem has the mood of the particular time of year.

attributes.title: bdff9522-d99e-4680-8b8d-cbfffffb88d8
attributes.field_text: all you who go and/ all you who come must yearn now  ̶  / for warm spring mists/ rise to hide those first cherry/ blossoms on Mount Tatsuta

attributes.title: ddf6ced0-f7a3-4f1d-88cc-1f7744ae0cb6
attributes.field_text: ah Kazuraki/ on the peak of Takama/ cherries have blossomed/ in the depths of Tatsuta/ white clouds cling to the summit

attributes.title: d18b81f9-a150-4b03-af0e-95972ce37d57
attributes.field_text: white clouds drift across/ the peaks of Mount Tatsuta/ where eight-fold cherries/ bloom 	did you descry which were/ blossoms and pluck them for me

attributes.title: fab8868c-234a-4569-9463-cd38a1f9c502
attributes.field_text: spring 	season of white/ clouds 	layers of new billows/ drift on Tatsuta/ Mountain 	surely the blossoms/ dazzle on Ogura Peak

attributes.title: 17c8484d-9ce7-480d-bb5e-07ea87d15e1a
attributes.field_text: those who do not dwell/ here in this village near/ Tatsuta Mountain/ where chill morning mists rise 	which/ of them could know autumn has come

attributes.title: b5296264-f672-48c0-9bc8-68c0b91dfcea
attributes.field_text: Tatsuta Mountain/ passing storms in the deep of/ night blow through the pines/ the clinging clouds have dispersed/ moonlight floods the peak they cloaked

attributes.title: 29dc0abb-259b-4da2-beec-e543ba087bac
attributes.field_text: as the tree tops thin/ growing ever sparser on/ Tatsuta Mountain/ the deer moving deeper into/ the highlands rustle through dry leaves

attributes.title: 559bff4f-e0ca-4d8a-94fd-32f1a0b6b835
attributes.field_text: Is it in the heart/ of the leaves to change colors?/ Why else could it be/ that the pines at Tatsuta/ are never dyed by showers?

attributes.title: c4c2b9a1-36a3-46d1-8dd1-c88f0196bad6
attributes.field_text: Are the storm winds/ Losing strength up on your peak,/ Mount Tatsuta?/ That never-crossed brocade bridge/ Seems to have drifted away.

attributes.title: 49c0716d-c53f-483a-844e-78ca57988b75
attributes.field_text: bright Chinese brocade  ̶  / is it to tear away this/ last autumn keepsake/ from Mount Tatsuta that storms/ buffet the unyielding boughs

attributes.title: 57dddd09-ae06-4bc7-b5ac-2e3090b96d8f
attributes.field_text: Tatsuta Mountain/ see these bright sleeves of passing/ autumn travelers/ when still the twigs and branches/ are unaffected by cold rains

attributes.title: 128dc7f8-1532-4f39-b187-ce9924ad7f3c
attributes.field_text: baseless rumors rise/ like clouds drifting high above/ Tatsuta Mountain/ destination uncertain/ I gaze in sad reverie

attributes.title: c5bd82a0-6255-4a5f-9d89-0b997d96ff76
attributes.field_text: as autumn arrives/ the hunters approach 	across/ Tatsuta Mountain/ while I 	whether standing or/ sitting 		am wrapped in sad thoughts

attributes.title: 1f1219fd-0039-4f04-b7a8-ae4872114060
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.229
attributes.field_text: River of Rumors/ they say that you flow through far/ Michinoku 	how/ painful to know that we must/ suffer from these false whispers

attributes.title: 2161e1cd-7468-4f5d-97ae-ad5c6fac8622
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.236
attributes.field_text: when I began to/ love you 	what did I intend/ to do 	if hidden/ logs floated to the surface/ in Rumor River’s shallows

attributes.title: e505c777-b02f-4407-8073-8bf273728cdc
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.377
attributes.field_text: Name-taking River/ of Tokono Mountain in/ Inukami 	please/ answer that you do not know  ̶  /do not let my name leak out

attributes.title: 9dea836c-4320-40ee-9fed-ae3d70c97e92
attributes.field_text: Natori River/ swirling waves above the weir/ clamor more wildly  ̶  / have the swelling drifts of bright/ autumn leaves damned up the stream

attributes.title: 0631d6f7-6b45-447c-b17d-ddb1205f0e9f
attributes.field_text: still alive 	no hope/ of meeting 	an example/ I’ve become to all  ̶  /oh 	to rot away like logs/ in Rumor River’s shallows

attributes.title: 9728f334-32f0-4e70-879b-3fdf93acc456
attributes.field_text: no reason to grieve/ now it’s all the same to me/ as Rumor River/ rises 	beneath its currents/ hidden logs will rot away

attributes.title: afd8a10f-4268-4b16-8410-42f5515a473a
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.222
attributes.field_text: my love swells like the/ buds on the reeds that grow far/ into the distance/ on Naniwa shore in Tsu/ but can my beloved know

attributes.title: 101a4dfd-e301-48c4-93a6-d686585ba2a9
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.235
attributes.field_text: Naniwa in Tsu/ will never hear your name or/ mine on the tongues of/ others 	do not tell that we’ve/ met 	and I shall never speak

attributes.title: be9b3226-6752-43d6-ac9b-41d1078f53ba
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.249
attributes.field_text: oh Naniwa in/ Tsu Province 	I know not what/ to think 	for here in/ Towa in Yamashiro/ I dream 	always 	of meeting

attributes.title: ce24324a-690d-453f-b23f-681ffe1b13da
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.306
attributes.field_text: as salty as the/ seaweed burned in Naniwa/ in beautiful Tsu/ are the bitter tears I shed/ so many years have I lived

attributes.title: d90d0dd5-6c4d-48fe-8b20-16ce305b9694
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.313
attributes.field_text: for a while 	it seems/ a fisherman I must be/ reaping the harvest/ of jeweled seaweed that grows/  deep beneath Naniwa Bay

attributes.title: 2e56e4bd-2b55-4771-9c81-92b929b33616
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.313
attributes.field_text: caught in the rain 	I/ went today to Tamino/ Island 	but I/ found no shelter in its name  ̶  / straw raincoat of the rice fields

attributes.title: 5c8b4556-1cf3-423c-8d82-03646d2759a9
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.329
attributes.field_text: at Naniwa Bay/ you scorned me 	my lord 	and in/ sorrow I drifted/ to Mitsu Temple 	where the/ fisherfolk gather seaweed

attributes.title: 5a27ae8b-ffc3-4d78-a46c-12d1909256e8
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.359
attributes.field_text: they say the bridge of/ Nagara in Naniwa/ will be repaired 	and/  then 	to what shall I compare/ this time-worn body of mine

attributes.title: 063b0568-b4bb-4f9c-9a00-d925ac1942fa
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.312
attributes.field_text: it seems the tide is/ now flooding in Naniwa/ Bay 	crying 	the cranes/ fly toward Tamino Isle/ seeking fields of straw rain-cloaks

attributes.title: cc53c8f8-58d0-4850-8d80-4e0c9416edbf
attributes.field_text: In every bay/ said to harvest seaweed/ the saltworker/ For what reason/ Do they go specially to Naniwa?

attributes.title: 048f0ccc-62c8-4167-8e76-398a9e86b757
attributes.field_text: Like a channel buoy/  bobbing off Naniwa strand,/ my name is tossed about./ But still I will come to you  ̶  / Though it be death to proceed.

attributes.title: 622559a7-a620-44ab-9b15-5da7f54772cb
attributes.field_text: Just like I [long for you]/  do you also long [for me]?/  The white dew/  settles, waking or sleeping/  my sleeves are not dry.

attributes.title: 0f9ab7b2-03c1-4b47-a502-f52558599e1e
attributes.field_text: Hiding in the inlets of Naniwa Bay that I saw just today, are those the boats that go out again and again and travers this world?

attributes.title: 0a6955ac-400d-488d-b629-e53e135f3ff3
attributes.field_text: Oh that I might share it/ with a person of true feeling  ̶  / the spring vista/  on the coast of Naniwa,/ in the land of Tsu.

attributes.title: 2f0c873d-0792-41b6-84a4-fe29a5013359
attributes.field_text: In the bay of Naniwa/ Seaweed-covered/ Gemstone rocks/ Appear-just so/ Does my love for her.

attributes.title: 97464cb4-7dba-4219-867c-38e059b5ee72
attributes.field_text: Because of one night  ̶  / brief as the space between joints/ on Naniwa’s reeds  ̶  / am I to be a buoy,/ tossed by waves of love?

attributes.title: 872956fb-aaef-4497-a2c1-aaefde1de95c
attributes.field_text: I’ll not forget it ̶  / the midnight sky in autumn/ over Naniwa/ even if I see the moon/ gleaming on another bay

attributes.title: 2c116fdf-2354-49cd-b8f5-68c9cfeed267
attributes.field_text: That spring long ago/ at Naniwa in Tsu  ̶  / was it all a dream?/ Now only dead leaves on the reeds/ rustle in the passing wind.

attributes.title: 61cca7ec-210d-4f7a-aeff-42984cc1abe3
attributes.field_text: ah 	poor gentleman/ had you but known what your life’s/ fate would bring today/ surely you would not have made/ that vow to Naniwa reeds

attributes.title: 21785ee8-8648-4717-a74a-ec08f57fff70
attributes.field_text: lodging in a hut/ where Naniwa fisherfolk/ light their smoky fires/ of reeds 	heavy are the salt/ tears that drip upon my sleeves

attributes.title: 5889b001-69df-492c-855a-818268e6f3af
attributes.field_text: why is it that I/ cannot speak my love aloud  ̶  / it burns within like/ the smoldering reed fires in/ bamboo huts in Naniwa

attributes.title: 421b82ce-5d4d-4c63-8007-f5cb51236349
attributes.field_text: Naniwa seafolk/ in what bay must I waste and/ die 	what connection/ to my past keeps us apart/ channel markers in the waves

attributes.title: 20cc188f-51d4-48ee-8a42-7a2478ccfdf8
attributes.field_text: never does a day/ pass when smoke does not rise from/ the reeds cut and burned/ to dry the soaked garments of/ the women of Naniwa

attributes.title: b5460a8a-a6d3-4e34-8ff5-4dac67b4072c
attributes.field_text: like briny waves that/ set the reeds to whispering/ along the shore 	how/ long will I go on floating/ through this sad inconstant world

attributes.title: c5869676-3b0e-427e-9ae0-ca3565478e2b
attributes.field_text: Evening of a new moon  ̶  / the tide must be rising/ in the Bay of Naniwa:/ over the young shoots of reeds/ crests of white waves.

attributes.title: 5e0dcce6-bfb0-4fd3-b160-81ccfe7e02e8
attributes.field_text: inexorably/ the world fades into winter/ at Naniwa Bay/ no verdant leaf is mingled/ with the scattered stands of reeds

attributes.title: c2d8cb5c-a200-45f9-81c2-f14bc9e9f561
attributes.field_text: at Naniwa Bay/ even the waves are hidden/ in soft spring haze 	yet/ a gentle light shimmers in/ the waters 	misty moon-lit night

attributes.title: 800ea24c-3a11-43a6-9e0e-dcc6dcf07f34
attributes.field_text: What are you saying?/ That I cannot meet you  ̶  / not even for a time/ brief as the space between joints/ on the reeds at Naniwa?

attributes.title: 5a5d1a6d-ea0c-4815-804e-de528d43b12b
attributes.field_text: at Naniwa Bay/ the long-legged cranes searching/ the sands at ebb-tide/ offer their cries of protest/ as the moon sinks in the sky

attributes.title: 0969fea7-382f-4b41-adad-010c70d8bc5e
attributes.field_text: through the night 	it seems/ the winds blew in the offing/ at Naniwa Bay/ the waves crashing on the shore/ echoed until daybreak came

attributes.title: d9c25a73-873c-4f93-924c-c1bc9261f5f4
attributes.field_text: […]on mornings when the flowers were fragrant at the Green Cave palace, on evenings when the wind was cool on the jeweled courtyard, they dipped into the stream that flowed from Naniwa Bay and determined which were muddied and which were clear, and they followed the traces of Asaka Mountain to separate the deep from the shallow.

attributes.title: 68f4d74c-a2e9-453d-bd85-e22b0ad228da
attributes.field_text: they were reaping summer/ grasses when first I came to/ live here 	for just a while/ I thought 	yet somehow autumn/ has grown late at Naniwa Bay

attributes.title: 643494dc-819b-421a-b6b6-6476461b7f55
attributes.field_text: the fair night deepens/ and 	rustling across the tips/ of the reeds 	winds from/ the bay add their sadness/ to the crashing of the waves

attributes.title: 98cb26b2-192d-4823-ac33-f1f995036d28
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.202
attributes.field_text: like fiery Mount/ Fuji in Suruga 	my/ yearning burns within  ̶ / an eternally smoldering/ passion my love can never know

attributes.title: f9233b64-127d-4346-b39d-c4751dd64e23
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.245
attributes.field_text: whether alone or/ together 	you 	my love 	keep/ my passion burning/  ceaselessly 	like smoldering/  flames deep within Mount Fuji

attributes.title: 4e198dc5-a523-4991-bc0c-4f3cf95601b5
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.353
attributes.field_text: ah burn brightly then/ bitter fires of hopeless love/ hot as Fuji’s flames  ̶  / not even the gods would quench/ these unavailing smoke clouds

attributes.title: fb6a8060-8572-4a82-9844-68b24debbf18
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.40
attributes.field_text: […] he could compare his smoldering love to the smoke rising from Fuji, turn his thoughts to friends when he heard the voice of the pining cricket, […]

attributes.title: a812f019-46f6-478a-9b0f-13f69c3984cc
attributes.field_text: Only longing/  I always do, Suruga/  Mountain, therefore/  Mount Fuji, only tears/  do I cry every day.

attributes.title: da08bf8c-ea9f-4731-9da9-ac974496f9f5
attributes.field_text: Is it just me/  that will burn out and disappear?/  As long as the world lasts/  The fire of my thoughts does not become reality/  just like the peak of Mt. Fuji.

attributes.title: 66f90398-0dd1-4cd3-ac69-36a89b56038e
attributes.field_text: Even if Mount Fuji continues to burn/  I can do nothing./  I do not know how to quench it/  my body not being water.

attributes.title: d29821d8-a881-45a7-9263-67a7b8d4e653
attributes.field_text: The furious gods/ Also know the flames of love:/ Must it not be so,/ That across the endless years/ The mountain Fuji burns?

attributes.title: 9a1c30ac-858f-4dfe-9d70-e29ebd08b6bd
attributes.field_text: A man of the mundane world/ Can never reach so far:/ Around the peak of Fuji/ The clouds rise higher/ As does my passion for you.

attributes.title: 24ffe6c4-c48a-444d-b127-96c652960cbe
attributes.field_text: Before I know it/ In my heart, sky-bound/ Is my love/ Above the high peak of Fuji/ Hanging with the clouds so white?

attributes.title: ce004454-9df6-4e17-9882-7afa38a913d7
attributes.field_text: Through all the passing years/ Burns Fuji;/ Far more than the mountain,/ Not meeting you, the flames of passion,/ Burn brightly in me.

attributes.title: b2780367-4608-478f-aaf1-9a0e3fcb6f3e
attributes.field_text: All through this night/ From the mighty peak of Fuji/ Have the clouds cleared, and/ Above the barrier of Kiyomi/ Brightly shines the moon.

attributes.title: 5ba8c473-3657-4ae6-b137-5a19c7785244
attributes.field_text: […]to the end of the year in winter when snow piles up like white linen on the towering peak of Fuji, […]

attributes.title: 8f4cff34-6ab4-47c9-be77-d2253c0cff68
attributes.field_text: in the heavenly/  plain 	gray smoke that drifts skyward/ from Mt. Fuji/ fuses with trailing mists in/ spring colors 	the sky at dawn

attributes.title: 64b0f050-2964-41b2-8585-a63ea7d6bbcb
attributes.field_text: At Tago Bay/ I came out, and looked afar  ̶  / to see the hemp-white/ of Mount Fuji’s lofty peak/ under a flurry of snow.

attributes.title: da113c94-50eb-4885-811e-d35edc2ae0c9
attributes.field_text: nowhere on the road/ could I ever distinguish/ the smoke that rises/ from Fuji 	for never does/ the hazy sky become clear

attributes.title: e680bca2-000e-4f21-82c0-8c42828bf51c
attributes.field_text: uselessly 	this smoke/ rises 	until it mingles/ inseparably/ with the clouds 	as the years pass/ I smolder like Mount Fuji

attributes.title: 73541826-1f10-40ae-ab35-794b235fbfed
attributes.field_text: my yearnings do not/ burn with the smoldering fire/ of Mount Fuji 	yet/ unknown to all 	alone I/ lie 	sorrowfully weeping

attributes.title: cee95191-72f7-44a0-97c4-cd1157144fae
attributes.field_text: higher even than/ the smoke that rises far/ above Mount Fuji/ greater still blazes the fire/ of my secret love for you

attributes.title: 61ce8c6b-b1f0-4b2c-ae7f-2397b628c007
attributes.field_text: igniting my heart’s/ determination to hate/ this sad world of ours/ the smoke above Mount Fuji/ must waft from my blazing thoughts

attributes.title: 16f8dd32-1ef4-4a77-9069-a9a5e22aa6e7
attributes.field_text: As smoke that drifts/ from the peak of Fuji,/ fading into sky/ with no sure destination  ̶  / so is the trend of my passion.

attributes.title: 9f78430e-33c4-4d06-8d92-9ac42e61967d
attributes.field_text: a peak ignorant/ of the season is Fuji/ what month does it think/ this is that snow should cover/ it like a fawn’s dappled coat

attributes.title: 2326c094-7e81-41b7-b331-e6be266c10f5
attributes.field_text: Sedge fields lie/ Around the estate of Fushimi,/ All long overgrown;/ He who passed across them/ Has left no tracks at all…

attributes.title: 3f674308-2aed-46b7-9a26-214f62f9835b
attributes.field_text: When from the sedge fields/ Of Fushimi at evening time/ I gaze across,/ A mere haze does seem/ The mount of Hatsuse!

attributes.title: 5356693e-7615-4121-b7cc-54a104d11cd9
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.75
attributes.field_text: oh mists of spring 	must/ you hide even famous Mount/ Miwa 	for surely/ in that holy place must bloom/ flowers unknown to mankind

attributes.title: c1f7a4f8-2038-4114-8c99-31f4ac34c366
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.273
attributes.field_text: how it awaits you  ̶  / how it longs for your coming  ̶  / Miwa Mountain 	for/ it knows there will be no/ visitors 	though long years pass

attributes.title: 26d85b2c-d828-4bcb-bac5-235d10629437
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.332
attributes.field_text: my hut stands at the/ foot of Miwa Mountain 	so/ if you long to see/  me once more 	come and visit/ at the gate where cedars stand

attributes.title: 9fbffae2-ca1c-4a2e-a6d4-4e8d70cc9b85
attributes.field_text: Even more than the mountain/  of Miwa, which I have heard/  only in rumor,/  even more cedars than that/  have I seen.

attributes.title: 49c64184-ee09-49c5-ac5c-602407ebee26
attributes.field_text: Long ago/ Might there have lived folk who/ As I/ In Miwa’s cypress groves/ Plucked a twig and placed it in their hair?

attributes.title: 9b8a5816-195e-444c-be64-0a748a21209a
attributes.field_text: On Mount Miwa/ Cedars stand sentinel/ Still, yet/ The one who told me this/ Is no longer in this world…

attributes.title: 7f18087d-b000-4f9f-8b6f-800da463491e
attributes.field_text: When I gaze across/ As sentinels there/ No cedars stand;/ Are you within the haze,/ O, Miwa Mountain’s foot?

attributes.title: fb2922ec-c5f3-4166-8571-701e4637b9b3
attributes.field_text: crossing Hatsuse/ Mountain as evening darkens/ seeking some shelter/ on the cypress-dotted fields/ of Miwa 	autumn winds blow

attributes.title: a6dd51ec-389f-48cb-9a89-7edfa6f1e2fd
attributes.field_text: who could have sent these/ seeds to one unfamiliar/ with the Miwa fields/ of cryptomeria 	her/ steadfast heart comes seeking me

attributes.title: fdca1dc7-4d41-49fd-9857-d9391a6510a9
attributes.field_text: shall I ever see/ again that one from whom I/ parted 	on Miwa/ Mountain 	cedars flourish 	would/ that I might bring back past days

attributes.title: 275fcf91-a024-4e07-8f67-28b84fbe6fec
attributes.field_text: this is a heart that/ knows not its destination  ̶  / on Miwa Mountain/ evening sky at dusk above/ the cryptomeria trees

attributes.title: 8fa15663-3f58-4982-9f3e-ec584d54a53d
attributes.field_text: to the dense groves of/ Miwa 	where they break off sprays/ to wear 	I will go/  and view with deep emotion/ the gate where tall cedars stand

attributes.title: 1bd84dea-b44f-4803-9b45-e2e3aea34148
attributes.field_text: Forever/   my long heart/  (like) the Yatsuhashi/  spider-leg, what I think/ will never end.

attributes.title: 8da8df7e-532a-4fbd-9247-6023279c9c42
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.267
attributes.field_text: heedlessly as he/ cuts the young reeds of Yodo/ in Yamashiro/ the one I love neglects me  ̶  / how fleeting my life will be

attributes.title: c1117cae-8298-492d-bc40-1dfb76b60d17
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.217
attributes.field_text: as the waters of/ Yodo Marsh 	where they reap the/ true reeds 	swell and flood/ when the long rains fall 	my heart/ fills with ever-growing love

attributes.title: cc0188f4-e512-4981-9e60-5b8873ac36bb
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.180
attributes.field_text: at the foot of the/  craggy mountain I make my/ solitary home/ white clouds hang heavily here/ pressing sorrow upon me

attributes.title: 5910bfd8-e55f-493e-8a2c-60f43e480b64
attributes.field_text: In the midst of night/ Briefly, will someone/ Come, I wonder?/ In the pools the wild rice/ Is disarrayed, this morning.

attributes.title: 4d7bff0b-2b06-4908-bb85-51c75ca9cec4
attributes.field_text: so deep the marshy/  waters of Yodo 	where they/ reap the true reeds	yet/ the reflection of the moon/ pierces clear through to the depths

attributes.title: e7e69686-e3ad-4880-a938-152a5ee7892a
attributes.field_text: brief are your visits/ to cut the young reeds of Yodo/ in Yamashiro/ do not complain to me that/ your flowing sleeves are soaked through

attributes.title: ae38fd3a-c8a4-4b98-98a7-617bf633698f
attributes.field_text: we hunted all day/ long and then spread brushwood boughs/ in Katano fields ̶  / now we see the bright moon in/ the Yodo River shallows

attributes.title: c65d643d-ce18-4767-ac5f-561bd87f8e7b
attributes.field_text: from the capital/ I set out just as autumn/ came 	mists rise over/ Yodo River	how many/ nights have they kept us apart

attributes.title: 15627bd4-47cb-466c-b0a6-e486f87f2969
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.43
attributes.field_text: in Poetry/ Bay 	the salt tides rush 	leaving/ no dry land at all/ toward the shore where rushes/  grow the crying cranes fly

attributes.title: a89ea409-5cc2-4c7e-9bbe-9f83e8819fe9
attributes.field_text: as plentiful as/ seaweed raked up to yield its salt/ the poems we’ll compose/ will equal our lord’s years 	waves/ rising on Poetry Bay

attributes.title: 25ff10e0-e22c-4dc4-9688-acdd7ee5e80f
attributes.field_text: at Poetry Bay/ no winds blow from my humble/ house 	yet in the moon/ is revealed the color of/ the wind that tosses these waves

attributes.title: c053d952-5a89-4470-af72-5140446a5f49
attributes.field_text: at Poetry Bay/ the moon rises in the sky/ as the tide floods in/ and the voices of the cranes/ call out sadly in the night

attributes.title: 5c0be008-9a06-4725-81ed-954ed34463ff
attributes.field_text: at Poetry Bay/ gazing through the green needles/ of the pines 	I see/ the seamen’s fishing boats pull/ to harbor near the branches

attributes.title: 8081c19f-7a98-4ef4-be5b-550717c20f65
attributes.field_text: at Poetry Bay/ drifting into the offing/ where tidal currents/ converge 	please let me know where/ I may find my own heaven

attributes.title: 34a0d491-c5d4-4b43-b095-965b92db01ec
attributes.field_text: Ōe Mountain/ the moon sliding down the sky/ sheds its bright light 	while/ on the surface of Toba/ fields the cries of wild geese fall

attributes.title: f6a19b3e-1795-4248-aea3-5dc04178fd77
attributes.field_text: awakened from my/ dreams by geese winging toward/ the little fields of/ Fushimi 	I see the moon/ From my hut 	this sleepless night

attributes.title: 0526051c-60d9-4dfb-9d01-8392b68aa94b
attributes.field_text: From beneath the pines/ of the Fushimi Hills/ I look out afar  ̶  / as dawn breaks over paddies/ where blows the autumn wind.

attributes.title: ed8d8679-c183-4d15-91ad-068b6e261c8b
attributes.field_text: even the path I traveled/ in my dreams has now/ vanished 	black bamboo/ snapping under the weight of/ snow in Fushimi Village

attributes.title: c1d07647-eae1-4d40-96e8-4ece4f9a9f9c
attributes.field_text: Does time pass/ With the drifting moon?/ At Ōhara/ The misty spring waters/ Are clear in name alone.

attributes.title: 34f251c3-8860-4ace-80ee-bf6005e0c6c5
attributes.field_text: Gathered/ Firewood for charcoal burning/ Warms the air/ On Ōhara Mountain/ The snow turns patchy.

attributes.title: 55f7a355-b108-459f-b0c8-115aff470c8a
attributes.field_text: dismal snow-laden/ skies 	as days go by 	even/ more oppressive/ smoke from charcoal kilns drifting/ over Ōhara village

attributes.title: 90623a8a-e93d-472e-b831-da031355803a
attributes.field_text: In the dark of night/ (one I felt would never end)/ You gave up and left;/ Did you hear the voice that cried,/ “Asakura! Who goes by?”

attributes.title: f49c79cb-9996-4f43-9912-d8d2789580ad
attributes.field_text: at Asakura/ when I am here in the hall/ built with rough-hewn logs/ whose son is it who goes by/ constantly calling his name

attributes.title: 65196eea-a059-45aa-8455-fb0a923eacb6
attributes.field_text: indistinctly 	yet/ it seems a new spring has come/ to the sky 	across/ Kagu 	mountain of the heavens trail wispy banners of mist

attributes.title: b3edb4c5-22e9-4dba-a80f-0b7a96561ca8
attributes.field_text: spring has passed by and/ summer has now come 	it seems/ cool white linen robes/ are spread to dry 	they say 	on/ heavenly Kagu Mountain

attributes.title: 32465cbb-892f-4d76-843c-ab0cd0f2a50a
attributes.field_text: surely now evening/ showers fall in Tōchi/ where Kagu Mountain/ of the distant heavens hides/ behind the billowing clouds

attributes.title: 4ef4c3b2-2256-43aa-b190-2f8fd425e67c
attributes.field_text: after the snows fall/ the true sakaki of the peaks/ are all buried 	and/ Mount Kagu of the heavens/ is polished by the moonlight

attributes.title: f6751a72-3366-4b9d-aa0e-2b2dd23b407b
attributes.field_text: Mother is away/ past Ōe and Ikuno,/ near Heaven’s Ladder,/  whence would come her letter   ̶  / but neither have I yet seen.

attributes.title: 6c21a69c-f14e-4063-8e98-8f4333ab3919
attributes.field_text: No gloom/ Would fill my thoughts, gazing/ At the sea at Yosa/ Were Ama-no-hashidate/ To be the capital!

attributes.title: aad67593-2553-4ae7-bb93-193bd9374b4b
attributes.field_text: The River Ōi:/ This ancient flow/ Have I come to visit, and/ Around the mount of storms,/ Scarlet leaves I see!

attributes.title: d1637118-65c6-459a-9da9-f9a0d9dfb7a1
attributes.field_text: if only I might/ gaze without endless worry/ if only bright leaves/ of autumn were not tossed by/ storms on Arashi’s foothills

attributes.title: 0bc070d5-9106-4ce5-9429-d9b78dfe2248
attributes.field_text: I feel I can no/ longer live in this sad world   ̶  / has it begun 	that/ time when I’ll grow accustomed/  to the stormy mountain winds

attributes.title: 761e5937-04b2-4f90-ad33-2c4df4e7a37e
attributes.field_text: now there is no one/ to remember me 	alone/ I vanish behind/ the rim of Mount Arashi   ̶  / bright moon in the daybreak sky

attributes.title: a23740c3-db29-45e1-8599-54bb62d5ade1
attributes.field_text: ah 	Akishino/ do cold wintry rains fall on/ that village in/ the foothills 	on Ikoma/ peak the clouds hang suspended

attributes.title: 0bdf8281-f2d9-488d-aa12-fc51af662bfc
attributes.field_text: I live only to/ gaze in the direction where/ my beloved dwells  ̶  / clouds 	do not hide Ikoma/ Mountain 	though the rains may fall

attributes.title: ddcb10eb-fa51-4bde-8f7f-ecf92c1bb254
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.165
attributes.field_text: today I left the/ capital 	 Mika Meadow/ and the Izumi/ River are in sight 	chill winds/ blow 	Mount Kase 	Lend a Robe

attributes.title: ef69f2c3-ef61-4395-9370-622e43573871
attributes.field_text: At Izumi River/ The peaceful waters’/ Bed I see;/ This year the shadows of the leaves/ Are truly clear, indeed.

attributes.title: 85e01f0b-d545-4290-b035-f93410e01ff6
attributes.field_text: On the River Izumi/ The water pools/ Around the fish-traps,/ Frozen between the rocks,/ Winter has come, indeed.

attributes.title: 37df5550-150e-49e9-95c8-30ac75cd2c58
attributes.field_text: though unmindful of/ the seasons 	even the waves of/ Izumi River/  have changed color 	a storm must/ be blowing through the oak groves

attributes.title: a6cbf7d0-363d-4e2e-ac9c-9ff8432a0b2f
attributes.field_text: Izumi River/ bubbles up and flows across/ Mika Plain 	when did/ I first see her that my love/ should well up in the same way

attributes.title: f09a81c9-c03e-46ca-915d-93250859412e
attributes.field_text: so difficult it/  is to learn to reject/  this world of ours/  but you begrudge me even/  a temporary lodging

attributes.title: b753deb4-2b86-44fa-b410-1e192cdad0c6
attributes.field_text: Egrets dwell/ Among the pine groves; how/ Noisy they seem;/ Their white plumes unpleasantly/ Echo through the house, it seems.

attributes.title: 4710ec67-1a46-4e98-9ecd-e108e8c9c3e5
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.54
attributes.field_text: not today 	do not/ burn the Kasuga Meadows/ now 	for here amidst/ the soft spring-green grasses hide/ my gentle sweetheart and I

attributes.title: 2745b094-32a2-4d55-9fad-01f1fa50ce3e
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.54
attributes.field_text: oh guardian of/  the fields at Tobuhi/ on Kasuga Plain/ go out to look 		how many/  days before we pluck new herbs

attributes.title: 57fb6c91-cb70-46ad-90d3-d62a339deeef
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.55
attributes.field_text: waving their pure white/ hempen sleeves 	beckoning to/ each other 	are these/ maidens bound for Kasuga/ Meadown [sic] to pluck the young herbs

attributes.title: 055dcda4-ecf3-4ff1-a2ed-32c3b0b2efe0
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.149
attributes.field_text: gathering young herbs/ on the Plain of Kasuga/ we celebrate your/  many years 	the awesome gods/ surely know how I rejoice

attributes.title: 395e099c-dce9-4dff-a893-931549d54d1e
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.164
attributes.field_text: I gaze across the/  endless plains of the sky 	can/ that moon be the one/ that comes from the rim of Mount/ Mikasa in Kasuga

attributes.title: 6ab1cf95-63b3-4b8c-823e-14173b9d2459
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.186
attributes.field_text: I merely glimpsed your/ beauty 		barely visible  ̶  / like the blades of grass/ sprouting through the deep blanket/ of snow on Kasuga Fields

attributes.title: 3909b381-192c-4917-8cab-bbe2904dc823
attributes.field_text: I would like to be/ A young plant shoot that’s growing/ On the mist-shrouded/ Hills of the Kasuga field  ̶  / Maybe he would pick me then!

attributes.title: e1a922bd-bfb7-4ae8-a267-44011f15d1b5
attributes.field_text: Ever since I saw/ The young shoots growing over/ The Kasuga fields,/ The depths of my own heart has/  Always sent its thoughts to them.

attributes.title: 0c2218df-3c59-4438-9154-b78e9ebb66de
attributes.field_text: When did it happen:/ It seems the mist has risen!/ On Kasuga plains,/ The snow has not yet melted,/  And I had just seen winter.

attributes.title: df69c232-6f09-436d-9204-4fc7b5e68618
attributes.field_text: The signal fire guard of Kasuga field/  saw it, so/  if you say there is nothing there/  you will commit a sin.

attributes.title: cb4d0353-143d-434a-944b-1b57ead79efc
attributes.field_text: At sunset, swiftly/ Will I come to call;/ When we meet/ That in far distant Tōchi/ Life was hard, I will recall…

attributes.title: 7dc8affb-caef-430c-9288-e7fc2e67f14b
attributes.field_text: On the fields of Kasuga/ Piled snow is all/ I see, yet/ Sprouting up/ Are fresh shoots.

attributes.title: 1a82e99f-a281-4010-b59d-2ad1acbe6824
attributes.field_text: beneath the surface/  of Kasuga field 	new buds/ of grass push upward/ as eager as my love 	through/ a thin blanket of spring snow

attributes.title: f6539545-531a-49c0-9bca-548985c98fd8
attributes.field_text: already the grass/ that covers Kasuga field/ has turned a spring green/ who has marked these fields as his/ who will come to pluck these shoots

attributes.title: 0c04eaed-7d11-43c6-821d-44a540dec15a
attributes.field_text: like white sleeves of girls/ plucking young herbs on the plain/ of Kasuga 	on/ Tobuhi field are scattered/ Patches of unmelted snow

attributes.title: 7fc53018-05bc-4ab1-a023-5112b3142827
attributes.field_text: which is this 	how shall/ I distinguish the fallen/ petals 	unmelted/ snow still blankets the ancient/ village on Kasuga Plain

attributes.title: bd940b36-c261-47a5-9bae-127c9b89c99f
attributes.field_text: even if we do/ not burn Kasuga Meadow/ the grass will send up/ new shoots 	better to leave it/ to the blazing sun of spring

attributes.title: f3d6e207-efa9-41f2-9bfa-282ae0660581
attributes.field_text: young murasaki/ of the Kasuga meadows/ imprinting my robes/ with a tangle of yearning/ boundless as this design

attributes.title: c9863f3e-392d-4837-8ae8-7400af032c4c
attributes.field_text: may your life last ten/ thousand years 	this I pray/ with linen streamers/ bound tight in the spring storms on/ the peak of Mount Kasuga

attributes.title: f1e9f0ff-f061-4bdd-8031-d9e9de2fb24e
attributes.field_text: is the heart of this/ god we celebrate today/ swayed by our appeals/ prayer strips ripple like wind/ tossed waves on Saho River

attributes.title: e99a0bf6-dda8-44e8-b176-5164a666db82
attributes.field_text: my waters hidden/ by these overgrown paths through/ Kasuga Meadow  ̶  / may the gods at least bestow/ their gifts upon my offspring

attributes.title: f44f21b5-d303-4b72-9a81-4d26cb37d86b
attributes.field_text: This world/ Has come to such a pass;/ In Kisakata,/ Fisherfolks’ straw-matted huts/ Have become my lodging!

attributes.title: 38b1b69c-0461-49f9-ad46-f100e0db67ca
attributes.field_text: a wanderer am/ I 	one who drifts through the world  ̶  / at Kisa Lagoon/ in the fisherfolk’s rough reed/ huts 	how often have I slept

attributes.title: adb99845-2afb-4cdb-a7be-c4e27e621364
attributes.field_text: The focus of my thoughts/ Are the river’s upper flows,/ Where incarnated/ The deity at Kibune, folk/ Transports.

attributes.title: 7771fe93-1272-432f-b464-676cdb8c8978
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.302
attributes.field_text: above the mountain  ̶  / Old forsaken Woman of/ Sarashina 	the/  melancholy moon shines 	how/ inconsolable my heart

attributes.title: 3d7b9e81-a3c6-4ae3-b84d-4dbccd114d42
attributes.field_text: this moon sheds its light/ on many places other/ than Sarashina/ mountain 	but inconsolable/ I am beneath lonely skies

attributes.title: 0bcdecd9-f426-41de-9605-b6d2371c5dd2
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.166
attributes.field_text: oh capital bird/ if you are true to your name/ you will know 	tell me/  if the one whom I love/ is  still in this world of partings

attributes.title: 5023fd23-5f57-4fba-b90b-f70afa56017c
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.41
attributes.field_text: […]think of the pine trees of Takasago and Suminoe as having grown up with him, […]

attributes.title: d39e8239-7fca-4dfc-b5e7-864e44ba95a5
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.110
attributes.field_text: autumn bush clover/ has put forth its white blossoms  ̶  / now will the buck high/ on the peak of Takasago/ Mountain cry out for his mate

attributes.title: dda5d615-a6d1-40a7-8c5b-ef4edb2efe8f
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.310
attributes.field_text: hiding myself from/ view 	shall I end my days here/ at Takasago/ in Onoe 	though I am/ not a pine upon the shore

attributes.title: b1465636-5d62-4d1f-b1ae-53bec51a6293
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.310-311
attributes.field_text: who then shall become/ my dear companions 	even/ the many pines that/ stand at Takasago are/ not those friends of long ago

attributes.title: cbb427f4-ce3f-42c4-b581-ef837d47e5b7
attributes.field_text: To the mountain guard,/ If I may be bold to ask,/ May I pick myself/ A branch of mountain cherry/ And adorn myself with it?

attributes.title: d84e6d7e-0d64-4785-ba30-2889c8d03a4a
attributes.field_text: The short summer night/ Continues to deepen, and/ It seems that I hear/ The wind blowing through the pines/ Of the Takasago Peak.

attributes.title: c9a56a49-db8b-4d2d-9a07-79355ad69c30
attributes.field_text: On Takasago/  peak the white clouds/  like this/  a person's heart/  I put my trust in.

attributes.title: 3c22d471-9b65-44d0-9ea4-600fd9c43b77
attributes.field_text: The autumn wind/ Blows hard, and with it/ In Takasago/ The stags/ Bell on, never ceasing

attributes.title: ee4aec7a-abd2-430c-91bb-c9e965e5f121
attributes.field_text: At Takasago/ the cherry trees on the peak/ are all in bloom now   ̶  / O haze out on the foothills,/ Please don’t stand in their way!

attributes.title: 55dacda3-3511-41d6-8951-13c2dde0dd4b
attributes.field_text: invisible is/ the color of the blowing/ wind 	yet autumn has/  come even to the pine on/ the peak at Takasago

attributes.title: 0eeae384-edee-4703-bcd3-982f7a8ae2fa
attributes.field_text: though even the pines/ of Takasago must in/ time become part of/ the past 	the autumn moon will/ be with you till journey’s end

attributes.title: 84899b94-b52d-4e52-b2ff-90935a6fa11d
attributes.field_text: in the lovely night/ beach plover’s cries grow nearer/ Narumi Lagoon/ surely now the salt tide is/ flooding beneath a tilting moon

attributes.title: 343b53c8-16e4-4351-ba46-8d2202af94fb
attributes.field_text: when fierce winds howl 	one/  plover 	tossed by suddenly/ churning waves 	calls out/ yearning for his distant mate/ blown far from Narumi Lagoon

attributes.title: 27323475-94e3-438b-b694-8ac909f152f2
attributes.field_text: those who live along/ Narumi Lagoon tie back/ their fluttering sleeves/ as nearby plovers cry 	they/ return 	and day becomes night

attributes.title: ae1741cf-4213-4244-bfc2-5d45d4ed3db4
attributes.field_text: I was born to love/ you 	yet languishing 	drooping/ like the red-bud oaks/ on the beach at Narumi Bay/ have I passed these many years

attributes.title: d56169ab-2e9e-41a0-9448-fbaaea2e6332
attributes.field_text: is everything this/ way 	floating wretchedly 	in/ Narumi Lagoon/ tides constantly ebb and flow  ̶   / but are they all that changes

attributes.title: ebeed5b8-d477-430a-8af8-96fa9ff32051
attributes.field_text: Cherries flower on/ Hira Mountain while/ Breezes blow/ All turned to blossom are/ The waves on Shiga’s shore.

attributes.title: b4e7541b-c454-447b-ab90-fed6346e7690
attributes.field_text: inviting the petals/  to accompany it 	the wind/ blew down from Hira/ Mountain 	now I can trace/ wakes of the ships that row past

attributes.title: b5e65e4c-5def-4da6-a40a-f03567a2284b
attributes.field_text: on Cape Kara in/ Shiga at Sazanami/ rippling waves are/ raised by the cold winds 	on high/  peaks of Hira hail beasts down

attributes.title: 4d6a09a3-f2a0-4667-ad7d-1f0ae54d2a62
attributes.field_text: in Sazanami/ the wind that blows from Hira/ Mountain to the sea/  Is visible in fluttering/ Sleeves of the fishermen

attributes.title: 9c7760c8-05e7-4926-bf0b-9a53e5ac9844
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.287-288
attributes.field_text: even the lifeless form/ empty as the cicada’s/ shell 	comforted me/ oh 	Mount Fukakusa 	keep/ the smoke spiraling skyward

attributes.title: a6d8eea8-b1f5-4703-ac07-32c7c86b80bf
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.288
attributes.field_text: oh cherry trees of/ Fukakusa Field 	if you/ truly have a heart/ this year 	at least 	you’ll be dressed/ in blossoms dyed inky black

attributes.title: 51721cc3-4f74-483e-8a35-feb8d7d7acef
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.328
attributes.field_text: oh Fukakusa/ if I go now 	leaving this/ village I’ve known so/ long 	will the deep grass become/ a dense and tangled field

attributes.title: 43612ab3-7a25-49ec-9439-c38f29d581d7
attributes.field_text: When the summer comes,/ Upon Fukakusa Mountain/ The cuckoo/ Calls most lushly/ Do grow excessive!

attributes.title: 28b53681-f578-4f23-8e1e-22ce84854b78
attributes.field_text: Daylight fades away/ and the autumn wind on the fields/ pierces to the soul:/ a quail cries from the deep grass/ of Fukakusa Village.

attributes.title: 39a91175-b262-40de-8c48-7e58a5447c64
attributes.field_text: a fragile vow as/ fleeting as dew on deep grass/ at Fukakusa/ yet autumn has returned 	it will/ not abandon this village

attributes.title: b0146de7-5e59-4acf-b155-bb4608f32a63
attributes.field_text: in Fukakusa/ village the moonlight glitters/ and the heartache too/ is as it has always been  ̶  / autumn wind sweeps through the fields

attributes.title: 7e09848a-23b2-4ed7-b72b-03cbb19156fa
attributes.field_text: as autumn passes/ my feelings and the dew both/ deepen 	visiting/ Fukakusa 	village of/ deep grass 	now only the quail

attributes.title: 47f692ba-d21e-43f0-a1da-e62f33aa2481
attributes.field_text: my sorrowing self/ fragile as autumn dew on/ the deep grass of/ Fukakusa 	has my trust/ Brought only these wintry blasts

attributes.title: 3a79a41d-648c-49f6-8639-b2a1e12a8cd1
attributes.field_text: night upon night 	so/ difficult to wait 	high on/ Mount Machikane/ I hear one song resound from/ beyond the clouds 	nightingale

attributes.title: f86e1ec7-6229-40dc-824e-5f16011601e1
attributes.field_text: At Matsushima/ On Ojima’s rocky shore/ Fished/ The diver folk: their sleeves/ As drenched as mine.

attributes.title: ea2a4e69-15dd-4417-9f2f-793efa8c7b6c
attributes.field_text: At Matsushima’s/ Rocky shore, the flocking/ Cranes among the reeds,/ Each and every one/ Has seen a thousand passing years.

attributes.title: a4372511-c8e4-4a38-a0be-58effd955a39
attributes.field_text: at Matsushima/ on the autumn sleeves of those/ fisherfolk who dip/ salt water 	the moon’s visits/ not only for those who grieve

attributes.title: 10a445de-a293-40ab-b8ea-0c6859636087
attributes.field_text: returning once more/ I’ll see again on Ojima/ in Matsushima/ simple huts of woven rush  ̶  / waves 	spare them your buffeting

attributes.title: db587cee-766e-48ef-b0bd-9c8d1f01d226
attributes.field_text: Time and time again/ Of his cruelty I’ve thought, yet/ Seeing him-as across Mikumano Bay – / I hate him, but/ I love him, too, it seems.

attributes.title: a9dd023d-06c6-4a09-80f9-eb4c41d9ea76
attributes.field_text: like the ships that row/ toward the distant offing/ from the inlet at/ lovely Kumano 	you have/ pulled further away from me

attributes.title: 3d655c3a-5745-4353-a516-00b4de96d063
attributes.field_text: covering the rocks/ soft moss beneath our feet in/ lovely Kumano/ mountain ravines 	if only/ there were hope for my future

attributes.title: 7a637a2d-e1c5-41c5-8c06-a3fd149b2d82
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.302
attributes.field_text: above the mountain  ̶  / Old Forsaken Woman of/ Sarashina 	the/ melancholy moon shines 	how/ inconsolable my heart

attributes.title: d6c7c5cc-800b-47a7-b068-40599fdc8498
attributes.field_text: You said you would come/ The moons and suns pass over/ Obasute Mountain/ And the mountain ridge suffers/  As I suffer in passing days.

attributes.title: e1bf7470-d9a8-444d-a75c-ca638ca5a050
attributes.field_text: ah 	Sarashina  ̶  / over Forsaken Woman/ Mountain hangs the moon/ of daybreak 	and ever at/ this hour my thoughts turn to you

attributes.title: 98537d4e-f739-4785-bb36-dc99b1a54609
attributes.field_text: traveling across/ Ina plain  	where the grebes flock  ̶   / on Mount Arima/ the evening mists are rising/ but I have no place to rest

attributes.title: b6a32769-a779-4610-8b29-e5b6744bed1e
attributes.field_text: Near Arima Hill/ the wind through Ina’s bamboos/ blows constantly  ̶   / and just as constant am I/  in my resolve not to forget.

attributes.title: cbe46970-0819-4753-84b0-68de73d5a8bd
attributes.field_text: "Composed for a folding screen in the residence of Nishinomiya Minister of the Left [Minamoto no Taka’akira (914-983)], to accompany an image of a group of women in travelling clothes among the autumn leaves on the path across the Shiga Mountains. /  / When I hear its name, / Long ago as now / This mountain is, yet / In the autumn drizzle / Are its colours supreme!"

attributes.title: 89e0389e-32e4-4ba4-9d9f-48fd8094b714
attributes.field_text: Sent from the Daijōin to someone in the spring//  if only I could/ show you 	here in the foothills/ Nagara Mountains/ near Karasaki in Shiga  ̶ / the scenery of spring

attributes.title: bf3a8f88-62ec-4c9a-9f53-f08f6e1b526a
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  there is no one I/ can count on here 	yet even/ on Mount Nagara/ when the night grows late waiting/ winds murmur through the pine trees

attributes.title: c36e6345-13da-4199-9599-d148365c3ee4
attributes.field_text: Composed on the conception of blossom at a former estate. //Wavelets wash/ The capital at Shiga –/ All ruined now, but/ Just as long ago are/ The mountain cherry blooms.

attributes.title: 36e11b57-59e9-453a-87c3-3cc0645e693e
attributes.field_text: Imagining ‘dusk on a journey’ for a poetry contest at the Poetry Bureau//  duplicitous is/ that evening smoke rising from/ Mt. Asama/ for I can find no village/ among mountains near or far

attributes.title: c17b56ba-ea38-4556-b69d-03510fb13a37
attributes.field_text: Composed on seeing smoke rising above Asama Peak when he had gone to Azuma//   above Asama/ peak in Shinano 	plumes of/ dark smoke are rising  ̶   / those far off and those near by/ must gaze on it in wonder

attributes.title: 30f513f1-a356-4e6d-8a67-8e3eb4f12c7a
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p. 359
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//   capricious as/ smoke clouds that constantly spread/ above Asama/ Mountain are you 	look into/ my heart 	then drift if you must

attributes.title: 1db0915e-f6da-4f36-848b-0980458262e1
attributes.field_text: Sent in the Ninth Month to a woman in Adachi in Michinokuni//  when I think of you/ behind clustering clouds so far/ away 	in constant/ drizzle on Adachi fields/ the bright leaves must be falling

attributes.title: 1a53b46d-92eb-4e9d-8109-e2ab89c4cd4d
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p. 368
attributes.field_text: A “torimono” song//  from Adachi in/  far Michinoku comes this/ spindle bow 	as its/ tips draw together 	silently/ come to me now and always

attributes.title: b5dd5020-a1f2-45a8-87ed-dde8eefbb6cb
attributes.field_text: When presenting a hundred-poem sequence//  an imperial/  hunt in the lovely meadows/ of Katano 	but/ hail 	you fall so noisily/ the birds rise too soon in flight

attributes.title: 8b578ed7-ea28-4067-8e04-5b25aea94c31
attributes.field_text: For the “Poetry Contest Held at the Home of the Hōshōji Lay Monk and Former Regent and Prime Minister”//  the plaintive quail cry/ on Katano Plain 	where stands/ of sumac are dropping/ their last scarlet leaves 	as/ autumn winds begin to blow

attributes.title: 0c3fcf91-6ed6-47d7-9d98-212e5caf1d57
attributes.field_text: One of five poems composed at the residence of the Regent and Chancellor//  will I again see/ the hunt for cherry blossoms/ on Katano Moor/ petals of snow scattering/ down at break of day in spring

attributes.title: 8b16e447-6cab-49ff-8d68-ada71035f82d
attributes.field_text: [About Falconry]//  Hail falls/ Upon the royal grounds of Katano and/ My hunting garb, for/ To lend me lodging out the damp/ Is there no one at all….

attributes.title: 16027725-c163-4012-b04c-127ee2aefc00
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//  Meeting is/  Hard; in Katano now/ Are you, and/ Your hunting home/ Seems the only place you go!

attributes.title: 044ce32d-dcbf-4457-b8d6-50e7385b2041
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p. 181
attributes.field_text: Katano.//   like the marsh water/ pent up 	no outlet for its/ flow 	thickly covered/ with the tangle of summer/ grass 	my heart has no release

attributes.title: f566b42d-b3c7-4f20-87c7-0d3c76d90ed8
attributes.field_text: When presenting a hundred-poem sequence//  so difficult to/ meet 	dew drops fall thickly on/ my bamboo-thatched hut/ in Katano village and/ on my lonely midnight bed

attributes.title: bcfab2b7-fa24-4d44-98ac-fa8d4d48b019
attributes.field_text: On ‘falconry’//  we hunted all day/ long and then spread brushwood boughs/ in Katano fields  ̶  / now we see the bright moon in/ the Yodo River shallows

attributes.title: 4dc89231-9fd9-42e7-a634-49c2d5a0c49c
attributes.field_text: Composed at a poetry contest at his home during the time he was Palace Minister//  an imperial/  hunt 	stalking every corner/ of fields readied for our/ search 	today too we passed our/ time in Katano Meadows

attributes.title: a49c7a23-7321-4996-911e-0a01620855e7
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  like that rock-built bridge/ spanning the Kume Road/ of Kazuraki/ broken in the middle 	will/ our connection also end

attributes.title: 8b635b94-6ce1-4e4e-97e1-373e11fd1d31
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  shall I never see/ her except from a distance  ̶  /a white cloud clinging/ to the high peak of Takama/ Mountain in Kazuraki

attributes.title: 7bc9d0b1-5b09-4e77-a5bf-1c7e25f4a4e9
attributes.field_text: Composed on the topic ‘fallen leaves’ and presented at the “Kasuga Shrine Poetry Contest”//  in the clouds passing/ swiftly by I hear the voice/ of the raging storm/ are they falling 	leaves of winter/ creeper on Mount Kazuraki

attributes.title: 5cc8d221-d4e1-442f-869f-1ff3c4021f52
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  Asuka River/ on the rippling rapids waves/ of scarlet draw near  ̶  /on Kazuraki Mountain/ early winter storms gather

attributes.title: ae803df9-e32f-4fd6-bf5e-9a613afd8be7
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  Asuka River/ bright colored leaves flow swiftly/ surely the chill winds/ of autumn have been blowing/ on Kazuraki Mountain

attributes.title: c191c56b-c201-4b98-a4a1-56fc3e43f2a9
attributes.field_text: From spring yearning for the first blossoms hidden in the mists rising on Mt. Tatsuta, the summer mountain nightingale of the sacred mountains yearning for his mate, autumn’s bright colored leaves on Kazuraki falling in the wind, to the end of the year in winter when snow piles up like white linen on the towering peak of Fuji, each poem has the mood of the particular time of year.

attributes.title: 1f69bb6f-88dd-443f-b2cd-ef61c366b61a
attributes.field_text: Composed as a spring poem when they were writing poems and presenting them at the Poetry Bureau//  ah Kazuraki/ on the peak of Takama/ cherries have blossomed/ in the depth of Tatsuta/ white clouds cling to the summit

attributes.title: 0e3018d5-61a3-4ba8-ac6e-8970745d6147
attributes.field_text: A spring poem from the “Fifteen-Hundred-Round Poetry Contest”//  the blue-green willows/ sway in the rifts between/ the banks of white clouds/ on Kazuraki Mountain/ the brisk spring wind is blowing

attributes.title: a97061c3-3d79-4266-99da-f889ef91bcfc
attributes.field_text: Composed on the spirit of the moon seen from within a valley, when at the house of the Hōshō-ji Lay Priest and Former Grand Minister [Fujiwara no Tadamichi].//  The shining moon:/ Does it make a traveller’s bed in,/ Bound with greenery,/ The Katsuragi Hills’/ Valleys’ river waters?

attributes.title: 79378236-4562-46cd-acac-fcc482e95a77
attributes.field_text: When Major Councillor Asamitsu was still of low rank, he secretly visited a woman’s dwelling, and when he said he would not return home with the dawn, she composed://  That bridge of stone/ Like our night’s vow/ Cannot endure;/ With the coming dawn, how sad/ Is the god of Kazuragi…

attributes.title: 451bac2d-dae1-4b4d-a7e8-38d1995fd71b
attributes.field_text: [Topic unknown]//  Jeweled climbing vines/ On Kazuraki Mountain/ Colored autumn leaves/ Only as a shadowy/ Image can I look at them.

attributes.title: a02b8cdb-be87-48d3-bf1a-3ba601783b1d
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p. 365
attributes.field_text: An old song from the Yamato dances.//  love is as constant/  as the dense never-ending/ snows that fall upon/ Kazuraki Mountain 	where/ I bundle kindling with vines

attributes.title: 33cafdb5-668a-4c36-8195-994538193933
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.374
attributes.field_text: A Kai song.//  the blowing wind which/ crosses the peaks and ridges/ of Kai Mountain/ if it were but mortal 	it/ could become my messenger

attributes.title: aa26b033-d576-43dd-9ef5-91808c415a80
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.319
attributes.field_text: Composed when he was Governor of Kai Province, for someone who was returning to the capital.//   in the capital/ if any should ask after/ me 	tell them that here/ where mountains loom above me/ and clouds never clear 	I grieve

attributes.title: eb245a21-af40-400d-b135-e8fdbae12812
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p. 296
attributes.field_text: When he had gone to Kai Province to visit an acquaintance, he suddenly fell ill on the road. When it seemed that he might die soon, Shigeharu wrote this poem and gave it to a messenger, asking him to take it to the capital and show it to his mother.//   I came 		thinking this/ would be a simple journey/ along the road to/  Kai and back 	but now I/ have crossed the final threshold

attributes.title: 8abf803e-c78b-450e-b2e6-8602328a2e51
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.373
attributes.field_text: A Kai song.//  how I wish I could/ clearly see the mountains of/ Kai 	heartlessly/  it stretches before my eyes/ Sayanonaka Mountain

attributes.title: fa3d7540-f479-4147-9ad5-5513141ca90a
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p. 167-168
attributes.field_text: Composed on the road when he was traveling in Kai Province.//  so many times on/  freezing nights my head rested/ on pillows of grass  ̶  / fitful in the dark I would/  brush away winter’s first frosts

attributes.title: 78ae4a0b-b1bb-41db-9aae-84dcb0555baf
attributes.field_text: When presenting a hundred-poem sequence//  no shelter even/ to brush off my white-coated/ sleeves 	halting my horse/ near the deserted Sano/ ford on a snowy evening

attributes.title: f7608cb0-d10b-4f6b-ba23-8e6480176872
attributes.field_text: Sent to a person.//  In the east/ the fishing bridge of Sano/  as it spans, so my heart alone/ what it thinks/  there is no one who knows.

attributes.title: 0f1ea578-08eb-4ff4-a5d1-e5cfa7351dde
attributes.field_text: When presenting a hundred-poem sequence during the reign of Emperor Horikawa//  even the weathered/ cypress planks are thickly grown/ with moss 	how many/ years now has it stood this way/ the Long Bridge of Seta

attributes.title: 0c15b37f-2e15-48c1-be31-fbced9375047
attributes.field_text: Included when writing long poems, etc., in ‘reed hand’ in a booklet//  others now have all/ turned their backs upon this world/ while I live on at/ Furu shrine 	what shall I do/ with this old body of mine

attributes.title: 2f8dc42a-310b-47c4-9d99-6d033d6b7b8a
attributes.field_text: On ‘long enduring a secret love’ for a poetry contest at the Poetry Bureau//  Isonokami/ holy cedars at Furu/ grow old	but there is/ no change in color 	neither in/ dew nor early winter rains

attributes.title: b48c7c4b-b3ce-4e52-b494-e8727bc1100c
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  in fields of Furu/ in Isonokami 	no/ grains have appeared on/ the ears of rice 	must my love/ too stay hidden in my heart

attributes.title: 89d794ee-0d01-4002-ab14-1721ce540a4f
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  Isonokami/ in Furu 	clumps of dwarf bamboo/ endure the frosts/ just one stalk of this year stands/ only one night still remains

attributes.title: 32e132c0-f619-424e-9bb6-203f90bf99e5
attributes.field_text: Written while composing a large number of winter poems//  the first snow fallen/  on the ancient Furu shrine/ buries the holy/ cedars	fields bound by sacred/ ropes hibernate for winter

attributes.title: 71e1f8cc-d2c2-412e-b6eb-feb29d9442c4
attributes.field_text: One of a group of winter poems//  deep green foliage/ unable to resist change/ what color will it/ become 	on Furu’s holy/ cedars 	cold wintry rains fall

attributes.title: 6d4404a1-76de-4e22-ae65-7660c08c1a85
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  tilling the early/ rice fields at Furu in/ Isonokami/ again and again 	I cry/ out against the end of spring

attributes.title: 2b6ea316-0388-4b00-9339-7436b18e36c7
attributes.field_text: For the “Fifteen-Hundred-Round Poetry Contest”//  Isonokami/ who was it planted cherry/ trees in ancient fields/ of Furu to become springtime/ souvenirs of one unforgotten

attributes.title: faffd701-d20c-42c1-af7a-a289a40be175
attributes.field_text: A long poem presented together with a hundred poem sequence in the same reign.//  In ignorance of the season/ Trees buried in the valley/ Do quite rot away;/ Long ago, in springtime/ How dear it was/ Now/ I cannot tell: just/ Upon the unchanging moon’s/ Light do I turn my gaze, yet/ Drenched by the showers/ Upon the beaches of my sleeves/ The tides rise high;/ In rain-gear/ Filled with pity,/ Folk to come calling/ Like upon the breaking waves/ The fishing boats/ Have rowed far away/ Into the common world, yet/ Since, to you, my Lord, my feelings/ Have I expressed:/ All my many cares/ Are forgotten ‘mongst the grasses,/ Forgotten, I live;/ At Sumi Bay/ For a thousand years the pine trees’/ Far/ Distant treetops/ Seem touched with glory/ Everlasting/ In which I may trust;/ On Nagusa Beach/ Did I find consolation/ Long ago, at the shrine of Furu/ That my/ Colours lacked for brilliance/ I had forgotten;/ Beneath the scarlet autumn leaves/ Does a trace yet linger?/ Aged now, as the sacred grove of Oiso,/ Yet you did ask me, but/ Now, I have nothing,/ All/ Is seared by the frosts/ And withered, but/ I have gathered together/ Brief daubings of my brush,/ With no sense or skill – / I cannot conceal it – / And that this must be my name/ O, I do regret it! A mandarin duck/ Adrift in sorrow:/ Is that to be my fate?

attributes.title: 2e416759-c78c-4af7-81d4-ffb4486375ff
attributes.field_text: He sent this to a woman he had met in Yamato.//  Over and over/ You are the one that I love./ Out in Yamato/ The old field with early blooms/ As they come forth I send my thoughts.

attributes.title: ff01a462-d3c3-4428-a025-28e776d9e853
attributes.field_text: Circumstance unknown//  Iso no Kami/ Even old Furu Field grass/ In autumn, indeed/ Especially the color/ Changes itself as if new.

attributes.title: bc3a056b-69a3-4046-8035-1bf48dbff9a0
attributes.field_text: On leaving Furu Mountain in Yamato//  The cherry tree there/ On Mount Furu, which stands in/ Iso no Kami:/ There is no one left who knows/ The time when it was planted.

attributes.title: ba1097dc-79e5-46a3-868b-55b7dc3871ec
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.348
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//  Hatsuse River/ there by those ancient waters/ towering two-trunked cedar/ after years have passed/ once more we’ll meet 	you and I/ towering two-trunked cedar

attributes.title: e97dc038-89f2-4b9b-a4f7-a8fa822386fa
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.304
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//  in the meadows of/ Furu in Isonokami/ withered oak leaves still/ cling to the trees 	so my first/ love remains unforgotten

attributes.title: 0aa250cc-a42f-43bb-9a52-fe9ac21f87a1
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.244-245
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//  ah the middle road/ that leads to Furu in far/ Isonokami/ had I not loved rashly once/ would I now pine so sadly

attributes.title: 6996475c-414f-4388-ac1a-97693c0a58af
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.161
attributes.field_text: Composed when the Ninna Mikado was Crown Prince and was returning from viewing Furu Falls.//  longing still to stay/ tears flow on parting now 	and/ mingle with the falls  ̶  / downstream they must be wide-eyed/ to see the waters swelling

attributes.title: 175df868-7287-4d96-9c19-c9d1acd5ccbc
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.118
attributes.field_text: When the Ninna Mikado was still a prince, he stayed overnight at the home of Henjō’s mother on his way to admire the Furu Waterfall and the garden was designed to resemble an autumn field. Henjō recited this poem as they conversed.//  perhaps because this/ village is desolate/ its inhabitant/ grown old 	both garden and fence/  have become autumnal fields

attributes.title: dcc0c3c5-b1cf-4408-bc10-58eaf01a55ca
attributes.field_text: When composing a number of love poems//  if only my thoughts/ could flow from my brimming heart/ where they’re pent as by/ the weir that holds back waters/ in Ide of Yamashiro

attributes.title: 4b341612-8d89-4d74-81ce-4c07f6b83ed7
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown//  scooping up the pure/ jeweled waters of Ide/  in Yamashiro/ I drank handfuls 	yet in this/ world promises are broken

attributes.title: 4bc91106-e628-486a-a592-8d716d04465a
attributes.field_text: Composed for the “Teijinoin Poetry Contest” of the thirteenth year of Engi//  on rugged far-off/ mountains 	yellow roses have/ already fallen/ surely the frogs of Ide/ must be crying sadly now

attributes.title: 69b051e7-22a7-4701-a90d-c934d3637f87
attributes.field_text: Composed for a hundred-poem sequence presented to the sovereign//  stopping our horses/ to drink again at Tama/ River in Ide/ swollen by dew from petals/ of yellow mountain roses

attributes.title: 1ffa6f95-d94c-4c39-8644-f99bf7ee72ff
attributes.field_text: Hearing that the same person had come from somewhere, she attached this to one of the same flowers.//  Unpleasant/ Thoughts fill my head:/ In boredom/ All alone (are you?) with an Ide/ Globeflower’s blooms.

attributes.title: 971589a8-98f2-4289-89cd-c1e91e2a518a
attributes.field_text: He talked to her for the first time//  In a hidden marsh/ lamenting secretly/ that is my body!/ Shall I become/ a frog in Ide?

attributes.title: 5d283c3c-a4a7-4ea7-a769-82edb0c7e1df
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.84
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//  the petals of the/  mountain roses of Ide/ have fallen and the/  frogs cry 	if only I had/ come when they were at their peak

attributes.title: a52bed92-96b9-4ff4-bc65-752843df1a09
attributes.field_text: Composed near the bridge at Nagara.//  All/ Does ever change, it seems,/ Within this world/ Long ago, at Nagara/ Were there bridge pillars.

attributes.title: aed67a10-2d15-4b0a-b673-1a0af264ecb8
attributes.field_text: At a time when he was seeing a woman, he had cause to go to Nagara in the Province of Tsu and sent this to her house.//  ‘Will he forget me?’ you might think-/ I may be long gone in Nagara, yet/ My heart is yours-/ My love/ I would never leave behind.

attributes.title: 22ac0a2c-1040-413e-a7e4-ed04ceb8b016
attributes.field_text: Takashina no Narimune, leaving for Naniwa in the train of Koichijō-in, sent a message saying how much he would miss her.//  For a little while,/ Surely, you’ll remember me,/ But in the land of Tsu,/ Once you’ve dallied at Nagara,/ You’ll forget me soon enough.

attributes.title: fc5b38fc-e83e-4b47-97dd-ad2b510582ae
attributes.field_text: Composed at the bridge at Nagara.//  These bridge pillars/ Were there not at Nagara,/ Should the current of the world/ Bring the name to one’s ears,/ Would one even see its traces?

attributes.title: 9320ed15-c5ef-4a86-a7fa-22de673538d8
attributes.field_text: Written beside [a picture of] the Bridge of Nagara on a folding screen [made for] the [sixtieth birthday] celebrations of the Lay Priest Chancellor [Fujiwara no Kaneie (929-990)].//  Never touched by decay,/ The bridge of Nagara’s/ Bridge pillars/ Endure and so/ Will you, I’d say.

attributes.title: 83af236b-1ce7-4a53-9339-6c912c7fe208
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//  Endless/ I thought, at Nagara/ Were the bridge pillars;/ But for all my love,/ Our time is done!

attributes.title: c736d2a3-e16e-4eb0-9f46-ec904efc9139
attributes.field_text: Composed to accompany a painting of the few remains of the bridge at Naraga [sic] on a folding screen for His Majesty, during the Tenryaku era.//  From between the reeds/ Can one see at Nagara/ The bridge pillars:/ A trace from long ago/ To guide us now…

attributes.title: ccccc4aa-1bf1-45c4-99b8-7b66f9d293a8
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.41
attributes.field_text: […] or he might hear that there was no smoke rising from Mount Fuji or that the Nagara Bridge had been rebuilt  ̶ At such times, it was only through poetry that his heart was soothed.

attributes.title: a4f304cc-9f76-418e-8c56-275ca7531523
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.305
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//   in this world 	two things/ grow old 	of this I’m certain  ̶ /one is the bridge of/  Nagara in Tsu Province/ and the second 	it is I

attributes.title: 49334f3a-9497-4f4d-a21e-281db855a143
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.359
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//   they say the bridge of/ Nagara in Naniwa/ will be repaired 	and/ then 	to what shall I compare/ this time-worn body of mine

attributes.title: 5384db19-0b5a-4b76-81d5-752a0bd3dc62
attributes.field_source: Rodd, Laurel R. and Henkenius, Mary C. (1984): p.285
attributes.field_text: Topic unknown.//   our meetings thwarted/ so long have I yearned 	that the/ days have stretched out/ like the Nagara Bridge and/ an entire year has gone by
